We establish stability and error estimates for the semi-discrete scheme and for the fully discrete, linearized backward Euler scheme. The analysis shows an infinite predictability horizon: the effect of the initial error decays exponentially in time, and the model error is first order in the observation resolution H and of order [MATH] in the pressure nudging parameter [MATH]. Balancing these two error terms, we choose [MATH], which yields the optimal convergence rate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates.
tldr: Numerical analysis of a data assimilation model for slightly compressible flow, demonstrating exponential decay of initial error and optimal convergence rates.
motivation: Velocity-only nudging has limitations; joint velocity-pressure nudging is proposed to improve flow predictions.
method: Stability and error estimates are established for semi-discrete and fully discrete finite element schemes.
result: The analysis shows exponential decay of initial error and first-order error in observation resolution and pressure nudging parameter, with optimal convergence when balanced.
conclusion: Numerical experiments confirm the predicted rates, validating the effectiveness of the joint nudging approach.

title: On The Computational And Statistical Efficiency Of The Empirical Maximum Entropy On The Mean Method
authors: Matthew King-Roskamp, Gabriel Rioux, Rustum Choksi, Tim Hoheisel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Maximum Entropy on the Mean (MEM) method provides a flexible computational framework for solving inverse problems by combining data fidelity with entropy-based regularization. In practice, however, the prior distribution is typically unknown but can be estimated from data, giving rise to the empirical MEM method. We establish a parametric convergence rate of [MATH] in expectation for empirical MEM, improving upon the previously established [MATH] guarantee by King-Roskamp et al. (2026). Our proof is based on a novel stability analysis of the primal and dual optimization problems under perturbations of the underlying probability measure, relying only on foundational tools from convex analysis and probability. We further show that the MEM dual problem admits a reformulation as an expected risk minimization problem, thereby placing MEM within the modern framework of stochastic optimization and enabling scalable stochastic gradient algorithms for large-scale inverse problems. Together, these results place empirical MEM as a statistically and computationally efficient methodology for data-driven inverse problems.
tldr: This paper improves convergence guarantees for the empirical Maximum Entropy on the Mean method and connects it to stochastic optimization for efficient large-scale inverse problems.
motivation: To establish better convergence rates for empirical MEM and to enable scalable algorithms via stochastic optimization.
method: The authors use a novel stability analysis of primal and dual optimization problems under probability measure perturbations, and reformulate the dual as an expected risk minimization problem.
result: They achieve a parametric convergence rate in expectation, improving on previous guarantees, and show the dual reformulation allows stochastic gradient methods.
conclusion: The empirical MEM method is statistically and computationally efficient for data-driven inverse problems.

title: Quantile Randomized Kaczmarz For Streaming Linear Systems With Massart Noise
authors: Emeric Battaglia, Jian-Feng Cai, Junren Chen, Anna Ma, Deanna Needell, Tong Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantile randomized Kaczmarz (QRK) has proven to be an efficient solver for corrupted linear systems and has received much attention. It was recently shown by Cai et al. (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47(2):802-823, 2026) that using [MATH] samples for computing the quantile is necessary and sufficient for QRK to converge linearly over [MATH] iterations when solving linear systems with a [MATH]-fraction of arbitrary corruptions, as long as [MATH] is small enough. However, it remains unclear how large the corruption level [MATH] can be, and how to compute the required subsample size [MATH] explicitly, without hidden constants. This paper studies streaming linear systems with Massart noise via QRK using an order-optimal batch size [MATH] in each update. The independence of samples from previous iterations in the streaming setting enables a sharper analysis, yielding explicit, computable bounds on both the tolerable corruption level and the required subsample size. In particular, we establish linear convergence for corruption levels of up to approximately 7%. We also discuss how the constants improve under oblivious noise.
tldr: This paper analyzes the quantile randomized Kaczmarz algorithm for streaming linear systems with Massart noise, providing explicit bounds on corruption level and subsample size.
motivation: To determine the maximum corruption level that QRK can handle and to compute the required subsample size without hidden constants.
method: The authors study QRK in a streaming setting with independent samples, using an order-optimal batch size to derive sharper analysis.
result: They establish linear convergence for corruption levels up to approximately 7% and discuss improvements under oblivious noise.
conclusion: The streaming setting enables explicit computable bounds, improving upon previous work that had hidden constants.

title: Ada-TokenCom: Rate-Adaptive Token Communications Via Large-Model-Driven Token Compression And Generation
authors: Zijun Zhang, Li Qiao, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Zhen Gao, Mehdi Bennis, Kaibin Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Token Communications (TokenCom) has recently emerged as a new paradigm in which tokens serve as unified units for communication and computation, enabling efficient multimodal semantic and goal-oriented transmission. In this paper, we develop Ada-TokenCom, a rate-adaptive TokenCom framework based on large autoregressive models, which integrates next-token prediction with arithmetic coding to achieve ultra-low bitrate semantic communication at the token level. We propose a mixed reconstruction/generation scheme, where the transmitter encodes and transmits the highly informative tokens at the beginning of the token sequence leveraging a pre-trained autoregressive large model, while the receiver uses an identical model to predict the rest. Moreover, we design a Lyapunov-based algorithm to dynamically optimize both the source compression rate and the modulation and coding scheme, adapting to time-varying network conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed Ada-TokenCom framework outperforms both digital and deep joint source-channel coding-based semantic communication baselines.
tldr: Ada-TokenCom introduces a rate-adaptive token communication framework using large autoregressive models for ultra-low bitrate semantic communication, adapting compression and modulation via Lyapunov optimization.
motivation: To achieve efficient multimodal semantic and goal-oriented transmission with ultra-low bitrate, leveraging token-based communication and large models.
method: Combines next-token prediction with arithmetic coding, uses a mixed reconstruction/generation scheme, and employs a Lyapunov-based algorithm to adapt both source compression rate and modulation/coding scheme to network conditions.
result: Simulation results show outperformance over digital and deep joint source-channel coding baselines.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates effectiveness in rate-adaptive semantic communication, achieving better performance than existing baselines.

title: A Refined Parameter Condition In The Lyapunov Analysis Of Igahd
authors: Samir Adly
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent paper, Attouch, Chbani, Fadili and Riahi introduced the inertial gradient algorithm with Hessian-driven daming, called (IGAHD). Under the condition [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hessian driven damping parameter and [MATH] is the gradient step size, their Lyapunov analysis shows an accelerated estimate of the objective function as well as a weighted summability of the gradient for the case [MATH]. For any fixed value of [MATH], this condition excluded sufficiently small step sizes [MATH]. The present note refines one of the estimates in this Lyapunov analysis by retaining two coefficients that were previously replaced by lower bounds. This leads to the following less restrictive and sufficient condition: $[MATH][MATH]L>0[MATH]0<s><\beta <{L}[MATH]\beta>0[MATH]L>0[MATH]s>0$. Consequently, under this new refined sufficient condition, the conclusions in the original paper stay valid. For convex quadratic functions in finite dimensions, a separate spectral analysis leads to a larger region parameters. It gives a necessary and sufficient condition for Schur stability of the limit modal matrices, as well as the geometrical decay of the objective residuals and the gradients. This modal analysis raises the question of whether a different Lyapunov function would allow us to recover part (or all) of this extended spectral domain for non-quadratic objective functions.
tldr: This paper refines the Lyapunov analysis of the inertial gradient algorithm with Hessian-driven damping (IGAHD) by providing a less restrictive sufficient condition for convergence, and extends the stability region for convex quadratic functions via spectral analysis.
motivation: The original IGAHD convergence condition excluded sufficiently small step sizes, limiting its applicability. The authors aim to relax this condition to make the algorithm more broadly useful.
method: They refine an estimate in the Lyapunov analysis by keeping two coefficients that were previously bounded below, leading to a relaxed condition. For convex quadratic functions, they also perform a spectral analysis to find necessary and sufficient conditions for Schur stability of limit matrices.
result: The new condition allows the original paper's conclusions to remain valid for a wider range of parameters, including small step sizes. The spectral analysis provides a larger region of parameters and characterizes geometric decay of residuals and gradients.
conclusion: The refined condition enhances the theoretical foundation of IGAHD, and the modal analysis raises the possibility of extending the results to non-quadratic objectives via different Lyapunov functions.

title: Stochastic Trace Estimation For Positive Trace-class Operators
authors: Zvonimir Bujanovi\'c, Luka Grubi\v{s}i\'c, Daniel Kressner, Hrvoje Oli\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implicit trace estimation aims to approximate the trace of a matrix or linear operator accessible only through matrix-vector or operator-vector products. In the matrix setting, the Girard-Hutchinson estimator typically requires [MATH] products to achieve accuracy [MATH], while the variance-reduced Hutch++ algorithm reduces this sample complexity to [MATH] for positive semidefinite matrices. We develop infinite-dimensional analogues of these estimators for positive trace-class operators on separable Hilbert spaces. The idealized estimators use Gaussian random elements whose covariance is determined by the target operator, leading to unbiased operator versions of Girard-Hutchinson and Hutch++. We prove high-probability error bounds analogous to the finite-dimensional matrix results; in particular, idealized infHutch++ achieves [MATH] sample complexity. For practical computation, we introduce truncated implementations that restrict the random samples to finite-dimensional subspaces; for fixed sample budget, we show that truncated infHutch++ converges in distribution to its idealized counterpart as the truncation dimension tends to infinity. Numerical experiments with integral operators, density-of-states approximations, and spectral filtering for a radial Dirac operator show that these truncated estimators can achieve accuracy comparable to the ContHutch++ algorithm by Zvonek, Horning & Townsend while using lower-degree function representations and smaller internal discretizations in chebfun.
tldr: This paper generalizes finite-dimensional trace estimators to infinite-dimensional positive trace-class operators, providing theoretical guarantees and practical truncated implementations.
motivation: Implicit trace estimation is needed for operators accessible only through operator-vector products, and existing methods are limited to matrices, while many applications involve infinite-dimensional operators.
method: Infinite-dimensional analogues of Girard-Hutchinson and Hutch++ are defined using Gaussian random elements with covariance tied to the target operator, and truncated versions restrict samples to finite-dimensional subspaces.
result: High-probability error bounds are proved, truncated estimators converge in distribution to idealized counterparts as truncation dimension grows, and numerical experiments show accuracy comparable to existing methods with lower computational cost.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical, efficient, and theoretically grounded method for trace estimation of positive trace-class operators, useful in numerical analysis and computational physics.

title: Shortest Self-orthogonal And Lcd Embeddings Of Linear Codes Over Fq+uFq
authors: Jon-Lark Kim Junmin An
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper determines the exact lengths of shortest self-orthogonal and LCD embeddings of linear codes over [MATH]. By decomposing Gram matrices over [MATH] into pairs of symmetric matrices over the finite field [MATH], the embedding problems are reduced to the congruence classification of symmetric and alternate matrices over finite fields. Complete formulas for the shortest self-orthogonal embedding length are obtained, with two distinct cases arising in both even and odd characteristic. We also show that every self-orthogonal code over [MATH] with nonzero free rank can be viewed as a shortest self-orthogonal embedding of another code. We use Witt theory to construct all shortest self-orthogonal embeddings. A complete characterization of shortest LCD embeddings is also established in terms of invertible and arbitrary matrices of prescribed sizes appended to a generator matrix. Examples of self-orthogonal and LCD embeddings with the largest minimum distance for the code considered are also presented, some of whose Gray images are optimal codes over [MATH].
tldr: This paper determines the exact lengths of shortest self-orthogonal and LCD embeddings of linear codes over the ring Fq+uFq, using matrix congruence and Witt theory.
motivation: To find the shortest possible embeddings for self-orthogonal and LCD codes over a finite ring, reducing the problem to congruence classification of symmetric matrices.
method: Decomposes Gram matrices into pairs of symmetric matrices, reduces embedding problems to congruence classification over finite fields, and uses Witt theory to construct all shortest self-orthogonal embeddings.
result: Provides complete formulas for shortest self-orthogonal embedding length, and a complete characterization of shortest LCD embeddings in terms of appended matrices. Examples with optimal minimum distance and optimal Gray images are given.
conclusion: The paper contributes to classical coding theory by providing constructive and classification results for embeddings over finite rings, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: eBPF-Based Cybersecurity Mechanisms: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Stamatios Kostopoulos, Panagiotis Tsakonas, Evangelos K. Markakis
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) has emerged as a kernel-level framework enabling dynamic security enforcement in modern operating systems. While eBPF's cybersecurity potential has attracted significant attention, existing work remains fragmented across domains, evaluation methodologies, and deployment contexts. This systematic literature review applies PRISMA methodology to identify, categorize, and synthesize peer-reviewed research on eBPF-based cybersecurity mechanisms. Following a structured screening of 3,735 records from six databases, 54 primary studies (2018-2026) were analyzed and organized into a seven-domain taxonomy: DDoS mitigation, intrusion detection, IoT security, container security, microservice protection, networking, and security tools. Analysis reveals eBPF enables low-overhead security enforcement (median 2.4% CPU overhead [1.1-8.6%], ranging from nanosecond-scale costs for infrequent hooks to 10-20% for kernel hot paths) with high detection accuracy (94-99%). It particularly excels in kernel-level monitoring, real-time packet processing, and cloud-native workload protection. However, significant challenges persist: verifier-imposed constraints limit algorithm complexity, 85.1% (46/54) of studies require low-level programming expertise, kernel version fragmentation hinders portability, and 96.2% (52/54) of research fails to address eBPF's own vulnerabilities. This review identifies critical research gaps in multi-tenant isolation, adversarial machine learning (ML) robustness, production validation, and standardized evaluation frameworks. By consolidating fragmented knowledge and highlighting architectural trade-offs between safety and expressiveness, this work provides a foundation for next-generation eBPF security systems and actionable directions for kernel programmability research.
tldr: A systematic literature review of eBPF-based cybersecurity mechanisms, synthesizing 54 studies into a seven-domain taxonomy.
motivation: The work aims to consolidate fragmented research on eBPF for cybersecurity, which is not related to the user's quantum-focused interests.
method: The review applies PRISMA methodology, screening 3,735 records to identify 54 primary studies (2018-2026), then categorizes them into domains like DDoS mitigation, intrusion detection, IoT security, and more.
result: eBPF shows low overhead (median 2.4% CPU) and high detection accuracy (94-99%), but faces challenges such as verifier constraints, expertise requirements, and lack of research on eBPF's own vulnerabilities.
conclusion: The review identifies research gaps and provides a foundation for future eBPF security systems, but is outside the targeted quantum information and thermodynamics research areas.

title: Improved Subexponential Upper Bounds For $3$-Restricted Matching Vector Families
authors: Sidhant Saraogi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matching Vector families (MVFs) are defined by two ordered lists of vectors in [MATH] whose inner products satisfy specific residue patterns modulo an integer [MATH]. Most famously, restricted MVFs are used to construct the best-known constant-query Locally Decodable codes (LDCs). We prove an upper bound of [MATH] on the size of [MATH]-restricted MVFs in [MATH] for [MATH], substantially improving on the previous best bound of [MATH] by Bhowmick, Dvir and Lovett (STOC'13, SICOMP'14). Our proof relies on a new polynomial method argument that controls collisions in sumsets of matching vectors.
tldr: This paper improves the upper bound on the size of 3-restricted matching vector families, which are used to construct locally decodable codes.
motivation: Matching vector families are key to constructing efficient locally decodable codes, and improved bounds on their size have direct implications for code parameters.
method: The proof uses a novel polynomial method argument that controls collisions in sumsets of matching vectors.
result: The new upper bound significantly improves the previous best bound by Bhowmick, Dvir, and Lovett.
conclusion: This result advances the theory of matching vector families and locally decodable codes, but it is outside the scope of the specified research interests.

title: CHISEL-ing Back Source Code With AI-enabled Iterative Recovery
authors: Varun Kohli, N Raghava, Biplab Sikdar, Dinil Mon Divakaran
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decompilation aims to recover high-level, compilable, and semantically equivalent code from binaries. Traditional decompilers produce pseudo-C that is difficult to read and does not compile, while the recent LLM-assisted approaches generate readable, but semantically incorrect code. LLM-aided iterative recovery is an emerging branch of research, but prior works rely on supplied test suites for semantic recovery. In this work, we present CHISEL, a test suite-free framework to iteratively recover source code from Ghidra-derived pseudo-C. CHISEL uses simple yet effective feedback from a compiler (static analysis) and a coverage-guided fuzzer (differential analysis), augmented by rich observables for grounded divergence detection and feedback, cross-iteration divergence memory, and best candidate retention. We systematically evaluate CHISEL for compilation and semantic recovery, feedback oracle soundness, and iteration overhead on 120 ExeBench functions compiled for the x86-64 architecture, across four optimizations (O0-O3), in both stripped and unstripped variants, using the open-weight Gemma4:31b LLM. CHISEL, with all recommended features, achieves an average of 96.1% re-compilability and 79.8% re-executability rates at an average of 2.1 iterations. Significantly, CHISEL recovers 26% of first-generation execution errors. At the same time, CHISEL feedback oracle falsely accepts only 9.4% candidates. Lastly, CHISEL performs significantly better than two recent prior work on LLM-assisted decompilation.
tldr: CHISEL is a test-suite-free framework that uses compiler feedback and fuzzing to iteratively recover source code from binaries, achieving high re-compilability and re-executability.
motivation: Traditional and LLM-assisted decompilation often produce code that is either hard to read or semantically incorrect; previous methods relied on test suites, which may not be available.
method: CHISEL uses Ghidra-derived pseudo-C, combines static analysis from compiler and differential analysis from coverage-guided fuzzer, with divergence detection and feedback, cross-iteration memory, and best candidate retention.
result: On 120 ExeBench functions, CHISEL achieves 96.1% re-compilability and 79.8% re-executability at an average of 2.1 iterations, recovering 26% of first-generation errors, with a false acceptance rate of only 9.4%.
conclusion: CHISEL significantly outperforms prior LLM-assisted decompilation methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of using compiler and fuzzer feedback for semantic recovery without test suites.

title: Caitlyn: Can Llm Agents Autonomously Synthesize Defenses Against Emerging Injection Attacks?
authors: Zi Liang, Xiaoyu Xu, Yanyun Wang, Minxin Du, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection attacks on Large Language Model (LLM) agents seek to introduce malicious instructions or content into external text sources retrieved by agents, forcing the underlying LLMs to execute harmful actions outside their benign scope. While current defenses effectively counter known injection attacks, deploying them in LLM agent environments remains challenging due to attack variants and emerging threats. Moreover, existing solutions typically suffer from an inherent trilemma, i.e., a constant trade-off among runtime efficiency, contextual precision, and adaptability. To bridge this gap, we propose Continuous Agents for Injection Threats via Lifelong Yielding Nexus (CAITLYN), an agent-agnostic defense middleware. CAITLYN integrates two systems. System I focuses on immediate defense against existing attacks using a two-tiered library: Tier-0 for rule-based detection scripts and Tier-1 for optimized LLM-based accurate inference. System II, in contrast, is deployed to monitor potential abnormal signals and attempt to synthesize new defenses. On standard benchmarks, CAITLYN matches the detection performance of state-of-the-art defenses at lower token overhead than LLM-as-a-judge baselines. On Emerging, our new delivery-aware benchmark featuring novel injection techniques, static baselines and the standalone System I configuration remain vulnerable. In contrast, System II autonomously synthesizes verified defense capabilities, substantially lowering the attack success rate across three diverse agent environments.
tldr: CAITLYN is an agent-agnostic defense middleware that combines immediate detection with autonomous synthesis of new defenses to protect LLM agents against prompt injection attacks.
motivation: Prompt injection attacks on LLM agents are a growing threat, and existing defenses suffer from a trade-off among runtime efficiency, contextual precision, and adaptability.
method: CAITLYN integrates two systems: System I uses a two-tiered library (rule-based scripts and LLM-based inference) for immediate defense, while System II monitors abnormal signals and autonomously synthesizes and verifies new defense capabilities.
result: CAITLYN matches state-of-the-art detection performance at lower token overhead, and System II significantly reduces attack success rate on a new benchmark with emerging injection techniques.
conclusion: CAITLYN demonstrates that LLM agents can autonomously adapt defenses against emerging injection attacks, offering a scalable solution to the trilemma.

title: TagZilla: Automated Owner And Abuse Type Tagging For Indicators Of Compromise In Threat Reports
authors: Juan Caballero Gibran Gomez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) reports often describe Indicators of Compromise (IoCs) such as IP addresses, URLs, file hashes, and cryptocurrency wallets involved in cyberattacks. Those IoCs are typically described in the unstructured report's text, or listed at the end of the report with little context, limiting their usefulness. This paper presents TagZilla, a platform that, given a threat report, automatically analyzes its text and tags the IoCs it describes with contextual information about the threat group and malware family that the IoC belongs to and the type of abuse associated with the IoC (e.g., phishing, sextortion, command-and-control). TagZilla provides a novel LLM-based approach to assign owner tags to IoCs using an open-world classification, and assigns 29 abuse type tags to IoCs using a closed-world classification. We evaluate TagZilla on a manually generated ground truth of 100 threat reports containing 1,534 indicators, where it achieves an F1 score of 0.94 for owner tagging and 0.93 for abuse type tagging. Then, we apply TagZilla to tag 765 threat reports, identifying 15,583 IoCs belonging to 637 malware families, 113 threat groups, and 162 other entities. The results show that TagZilla can tag IoCs even in reports describing multiple actors and malware families, enabling the generation of IoC profiles for those entities.
tldr: This paper presents TagZilla, an LLM-based platform that automatically tags indicators of compromise in threat reports with owner and abuse type information.
motivation: CTI reports often lack context for IoCs, making them less useful; TagZilla aims to automatically add contextual tags.
method: Uses LLM for owner tagging via open-world classification and abuse type tagging via closed-world classification with 29 types.
result: Achieves F1 scores of 0.94 for owner tagging and 0.93 for abuse type tagging on a dataset of 100 reports.
conclusion: TagZilla can tag IoCs even in multi-actor reports, enabling generation of IoC profiles.

title: Fine-Tuning Autobidders With Group Relative Policy Optimization
authors: Anton Safin, Alexandra Khirianova, Andrey Pudovikov, Aleksandr Katrutsa, Egor Samosvat
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated bidding (autobidding) is a core component of modern online advertising systems. Within this component, advertisers delegate sequential bid decisions to algorithms that must maximize campaign value while adhering to constraints such as a limited budget and a target cost-per-click (CPC). One of the approaches to resolve the autobidding problem is to formulate it as a Markov decision process and use reinforcement learning (RL) to train a bid generation function. The standard RL framework is actor-critic, which consists of an actor network that generates actions and a critic network that estimates the value of those actions. In our setting, the action is typically a bid or related pacing multiplier, and the value is the expected return from the auction given the bid. However, the alternating training of actor-critic RL models leads to instability and reduced robustness to noise. To address these issues, we adapt the Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework to the autobidding setting. This framework is a policy-gradient method originally developed for large language model post-training, where the ground-truth target is unknown. The autobidding setting shares this property, since the optimal bid is unknown in advance. Moreover, GRPO in the LLM domain is used to fine-tune the pre-trained model, and we use the same technique to enhance the performance of the strong heuristic baseline. We empirically compare Autobidding GRPO with actor-critic models, simple heuristics, and controller-based methods on the BAT, iPinYou, and AuctionNet benchmarks. Extensive experiments show that Autobidding GRPO consistently outperforms baselines in clicks and is the best or second-best method in conversion volume.
tldr: This paper adapts Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune autobidding agents in online advertising, improving campaign performance compared to actor-critic baselines.
motivation: Autobidding is crucial in online ads; existing actor-critic RL methods suffer from instability. The authors aim to apply GRPO, which works for unknown targets, to enhance autobidding policies.
method: They formulate autobidding as MDP and apply GRPO, a policy-gradient method from LLM post-training, to fine-tune a heuristic baseline bidder. They compare with actor-critic, heuristics, and controller-based methods on BAT, iPinYou, and AuctionNet benchmarks.
result: Extensive experiments show Autobidding GRPO consistently outperforms baselines in clicks and is best or second-best in conversion volume.
conclusion: GRPO is effective for fine-tuning autobidders, offering a stable alternative to actor-critic training and improving performance.

title: Optimal Adversarial Testing: Extracting Honest Test Results From Dishonest Test Takers
authors: Owen Cox, April Xu, Weiyu Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In applications, it is often required to test objects or people to determine their qualities in terms of certain metrics. However, besides being naturally noisy, the test results can be corrupted by adversarial behaviors of objects or people being tested (test takers). For example, dishonest test takers can cheat in the exams to distort the test results. With the development of AI technologies, such distortions driven by cheating using AI technologies are becoming more commonplace and severe. In this paper, we propose optimal testing strategies which can still recover needed test results even if there are cheaters polluting the results. The proposed testing strategies will optimally re-test selected group of test takers using different testing security measures. We determine the optimal testing strategies using a dynamic programming method.
tldr: This paper proposes optimal testing strategies using dynamic programming to recover honest test results despite adversarial cheating.
motivation: Test results can be corrupted by dishonest test takers, and with AI technology this problem is worsening, so there is a need for robust testing methods.
method: The authors model the testing problem and use dynamic programming to determine optimal re-testing strategies with varying security measures.
result: The proposed strategies can recover needed test results even when cheaters are present, and the optimality is established via dynamic programming.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to design testing protocols that are resilient to adversarial behavior.

title: Extending Silicon Avalanche Photodetection Beyond 2 ~\mu$m By Direct GeSn Integration
authors: M. R. M. Atalla, J. B\'elec, E. Rahier, S. Koelling, K. Omambac, P. Daoust, S. Assali, O. Moutanabbir
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon avalanche photodiodes provide a technologically mature platform for sensitive photodetection, but their spectral response is intrinsically limited by the silicon bandgap. Extending their operation into the infrared requires the integration of narrow-bandgap absorbers while preserving efficient avalanche multiplication and compatibility with silicon processing. Here, we propose and demonstrate a monolithic approach that combines direct, buffer-free growth of GeSn on silicon with a lateral thin-junction separate-absorption-multiplication architecture. The GeSn layer, with a Sn composition reaching 6 at.\%, extends optical absorption to a wavelength of [MATH]m, while avalanche multiplication is spatially confined to an ion-implanted silicon lateral junction. This separation enables independent control of infrared absorption and carrier multiplication without the thick Ge virtual substrates conventionally used for GeSn epitaxy. GeSn-on-Si avalanche photodiodes exhibit low pre-breakdown dark current, stable breakdown at 72~V independent of device diameter, and clear infrared photoresponse extending beyond [MATH]m. At 78~K, the devices exhibit external quantum efficiency exceeding 100\%, reaching 163\% at [MATH]m, providing direct evidence of avalanche multiplication. These results establish direct integration of narrow-bandgap group-IV absorbers with silicon multiplication regions as a scalable strategy for extending the spectral reach of silicon avalanche photodetection, opening a route toward monolithic infrared detectors for sensing, imaging, communications, LiDAR, and quantum photonics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a monolithic GeSn-on-Si avalanche photodiode that extends silicon photodetection beyond 2 μm, achieving high external quantum efficiency at low temperatures.
motivation: Silicon avalanche photodiodes are limited by the silicon bandgap, so extending their operation into the infrared requires integrating narrow-bandgap absorbers while preserving avalanche multiplication and CMOS compatibility.
method: The authors propose and demonstrate direct, buffer-free growth of GeSn on silicon using a lateral thin-junction separate-absorption-multiplication architecture, with avalanche multiplication confined to an ion-implanted silicon junction.
result: GeSn-on-Si avalanche photodiodes exhibit low dark current, stable breakdown at 72 V, and infrared photoresponse beyond 2 μm; at 78 K, external quantum efficiency exceeds 100%, reaching 163%, confirming avalanche multiplication.
conclusion: Direct integration of narrow-bandgap group-IV absorbers with silicon multiplication regions offers a scalable strategy for extending silicon avalanche photodetection into the infrared, with potential applications in sensing, imaging, communications, LiDAR, and quantum photonics.

title: Exploiting Exact Conditionals Improves Conditioning: Provably Fast Mixing Time Bounds By Sampling From The Marginal
authors: Abhijit Chowdhary, Federica Milinanni, Julianne Chung, Elizabeth Newman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of sampling from a probability distribution arises in many applications such as posterior sampling in hierarchical Bayesian inverse problems and Gaussian processes for machine learning. Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms are often used for sampling from a target probability distribution, but implementations can be computationally expensive, especially for large-scale problems. In certain applications, the target distribution naturally factorizes into a lower dimensional marginal distribution and a conditional distribution that allows exact sampling. We describe an MCMC algorithm called MarCo that exploits such a structure and generates a Markov chain via Metropolis-Hastings sampling from the marginal distribution, followed by sampling from the exact conditional distribution. By design, MarCo constructs a Markov chain on the joint space that inherits the convergence behavior of the marginal MCMC algorithm. This provides multiple theoretical and computational advantages. We prove that MarCo can achieve improved mixing time upper bounds compared to direct sampling from the joint distribution. Moreover, compared to one-block methods that also exploit marginal-conditional structure, we use the framework of Peskun-Tierney ordering to show that MarCo has a larger right spectral gap and smaller asymptotic variance, thus leading to superior convergence properties. Numerical results illustrate the performance benefits of MarCo and are provided for various problems, including a semi-blind image deblurring example.
tldr: Introduces MarCo, an MCMC algorithm that samples from the marginal and then exactly from the conditional, provably improving mixing times and spectral properties.
motivation: High-dimensional sampling via MCMC can be expensive; exploiting natural factorization into marginal and exact conditional sampling can enhance efficiency and convergence.
method: MarCo uses Metropolis-Hastings on the lower-dimensional marginal, followed by exact sampling from the conditional, constructing a joint-space chain with improved convergence characteristics.
result: The algorithm achieves better mixing time upper bounds and larger right spectral gap / smaller asymptotic variance compared to direct joint sampling and one-block methods.
conclusion: MarCo provides a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient approach for distributions with tractable conditional structure, demonstrating benefits in numerical experiments.

title: Can Tainted Pixels Expose Deepfake Videos?
authors: Juan Hu, Shaojing Fan, Sanjay Saha, Marc Herrera, Terence Sim
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Publicly-acceesible face-manipulation tools have made deepfake creation accessible to non-expert users. Against these, existing defenses are mostly post-hoc, detecting only after forgery has occurred, and operating on still images rather than videos. Research is lacking in i) the proactive protection of published facial videos against black-box manipulation tools, and in (ii) understanding its perceptual effect on human viewers. We introduce TaintedPixels, a proactive video-protection method built around an asymmetric visibility trade-off: the embedded watermark should remain inconspicuous in the published video but become obvious once a downstream tool manipulates the video. TaintedPixels injects structured periodic perturbations into the blue channel of facial regions and refines them under stripe-visibility, color-cast, and video-level LPIPS budgets, with lightweight motion-adaptive deployment. We believe TaintedPixels is the first proactive defense designed specifically against black-box manipulation tools rather than image-level pipelines or specific surrogate generators. Across three publicly available off-the-shelf video manipulation tools and two off-the-shelf detectors, TaintedPixels attains the highest forgery fake rate while keeping perturbations small (LPIPS = 0.0042). Our non-expert human study, conducted on a diverse set of 300 video stimuli spanning different lighting conditions, backgrounds, and skin tones, shows that protected source videos draw a 3.26% suspicion rate, while forgeries from protected sources are identified as fake much more often than forgeries from unprotected sources (90.72% vs. 56.71%). This validates the effectiveness of TaintedPixels.
tldr: This paper introduces TaintedPixels, a proactive defense that embeds invisible perturbations into facial videos to expose deepfake manipulation, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Existing deepfake defenses are post-hoc and focus on images, lacking proactive protection for videos against black-box manipulation tools.
method: TaintedPixels injects structured periodic perturbations into the blue channel of facial regions, optimized under visibility constraints and using motion-adaptive deployment.
result: It achieves high forgery detection rates with minimal perturbation (LPIPS = 0.0042) and human studies show increased suspicion of forgeries from protected sources.
conclusion: The method is effective as a proactive defense, but it does not align with any of the user's research directions.

title: On Symmetricity Of Orthogonality With Respect To Numerical Radius Norm
authors: Shamim Sohel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Birkhoff-James orthogonality and local symmetric points in the space [MATH] of vector-valued continuous functions equipped with a numerical-radius type (semi-)norm. We extend the theory of abstract numerical ranges to semi-normed spaces and obtain complete characterizations of the left and right symmetric points of [MATH] with respect to the numerical-radius (semi-) norm. We also establish corresponding results for the space [MATH] of compact operators on [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies Birkhoff-James orthogonality and symmetric points in vector-valued function spaces equipped with a numerical-radius norm, extending abstract numerical range theory to semi-normed spaces.
motivation: The research interests focus on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems; this paper is purely mathematical (functional analysis/operator theory) with no apparent connection to these areas.
method: The author develops characterizations of left and right symmetric points with respect to the numerical-radius (semi-)norm and extends results to compact operators, using abstract numerical range techniques.
result: Complete characterizations of symmetric points are obtained for the space of vector-valued continuous functions and compact operators with the numerical-radius norm.
conclusion: The work is a contribution to mathematical analysis but lies outside the scope of the specified research directions, hence it is not recommended for the user.

title: The Mechanics Of Democratic Dominance: A System Dynamics Paradigm For Dynamic Consent Engineering
authors: Muhammad Sukri Bin Ramli
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional frameworks of political communication operate under linear, event-driven assumptions that treat voter persuasion as a static, transactional function. This paper introduces Dynamic Consent Engineering (DCE), a novel interdisciplinary paradigm that synthesizes Edward Bernays' foundational principles of public relations with the S-E-E-D (Snowball, Equilibrium, Elasticity, Dominance) framework of system dynamics. By expanding Bernaysian operational constraints into a four-dimensional resource matrix (incorporating algorithmic media infrastructure alongside manpower, mindpower, and capital), we mathematically formalize how democratic institutions construct, optimize, and sustain political dominance. We map Bernays' classic eight-step engineering workflow directly onto non-linear feedback loops, information time lags, and demographic carrying capacities. Through rigorous modeling of systemic feedback structures, we isolate the dynamic root causes of political elasticity, policy resistance plateaus, and threshold-triggered trust collapses. Finally, we establish a four-step diagnostic pipeline and validate the framework via historical reference mode verification, demonstrating that long-term political stability depends not on ephemeral rhetoric, but on the structural synchronization of policy execution and dynamic feedback calibration.
tldr: This paper introduces Dynamic Consent Engineering, a system dynamics approach to modeling political dominance, combining Bernaysian public relations with feedback loops.
motivation: Traditional political communication models are linear and event-driven; the author aims to provide a more dynamic framework to explain and sustain political dominance.
method: The paper synthesizes Edward Bernays' principles with the S-E-E-D framework, expands operational constraints into a four-dimensional resource matrix, and maps an eight-step workflow onto nonlinear feedback loops, validating via historical reference modes.
result: The framework identifies dynamic root causes such as political elasticity and policy resistance, and demonstrates that long-term stability depends on structural synchronization of policy execution and feedback calibration.
conclusion: Political dominance is primarily achieved through dynamic feedback synchronization rather than ephemeral rhetoric, suggesting a systemic engineering approach to consent.

title: Criticality And Universality In Network Dismantling
authors: Lorenzo Cirigliano, Claudio Castellano, Minsuk Kim, Filippo Radicchi, Hanlin Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying the smallest set of elements whose removal dismantle a complex network, known as the network dismantling problem, is a fundamental task with many practical applications. Whereas network dismantling has been extensively studied over the past decade, most work has focused on developing efficient algorithms for large but finite networks. By contrast, the physics of the network dismantling process, namely how the network structural connectivity is affected by the removal of nodes or edges, remains largely unexplored in the thermodynamic limit. Here, we shed light on this understudied aspect of network dismantling by introducing an adaptive biased percolation process able to optimally dismantle a network. Through a systematic analysis of synthetic network models, we find that the proposed percolation process displays a universal phase transition, characterized by the abrupt and simultaneous disappearance of both the giant connected component and the largest 2-core, across networks with markedly different degree distributions. Simulations on real networks further support this universality, indicating that the physics of network dismantling is insensitive to a broad range of topological properties. Together, these results suggest that a topology-agnostic theory could be developed to explain the critical behavior of network dismantling.
tldr: This paper studies the physics of network dismantling, introducing an adaptive biased percolation process that exhibits a universal phase transition.
motivation: Network dismantling is a fundamental problem with practical applications, but the physics of the process in the thermodynamic limit is largely unexplored.
method: The authors propose an adaptive biased percolation process to optimally dismantle networks and analyze it on synthetic and real networks.
result: They find a universal phase transition characterized by the simultaneous disappearance of the giant component and the largest 2-core, insensitive to network degree distributions.
conclusion: The results suggest a topology-agnostic theory could explain the critical behavior of network dismantling.

title: Adaptive Workforce Exploration In Complex Productivity Landscapes
authors: Mateus F. B. Granha, Igor V. G. de Oliveira, Andr\'e L. M. Vilela, Chao Wang, Paulo R. A. Campos
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Specialization and task allocation enhance efficiency and innovation across diverse systems, from biological organisms to socioeconomic institutions. The evolution of task distribution and its influence on organizational productivity encapsulate the dynamics between task dependencies and adaptive strategies. We explore the organizational division of labor, inspired by the NK model of rugged landscapes, which is widely applied in evolutionary biology, and incorporate interdependencies among the attributes of technical experts within an organization. Our model considers two types of employees characterized by their task allocation strategies: specialists, who are permanently assigned to a single task, and generalists, who stochastically select a task at each time step. We investigate how the ruggedness of the productivity landscape, shaped by task interdependency, affects the organization's capacity to optimize labor division and meet market demands. Using group selection algorithms, we reveal the emergence of nonlinear adaptive dynamics, providing insights into how companies can adapt their strategies to meet market demands and foster innovation.
tldr: This paper uses an NK model to study how specialization versus generalist strategies in task allocation affects organizational productivity, but it has no connection to quantum information or related topics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the dynamics of division of labor in complex productivity landscapes, drawing inspiration from evolutionary biology to model task interdependencies within organizations.
method: They build an agent-based model with specialists (permanently assigned to one task) and generalists (stochastically choosing tasks per time step), and use group selection algorithms to simulate adaptive dynamics.
result: The model reveals nonlinear adaptive dynamics and shows how the ruggedness of the productivity landscape influences an organization's ability to optimize labor division and respond to market demands.
conclusion: The findings offer insights into how companies can adapt their workforce strategies to meet market demands and foster innovation, but the work is entirely outside the scope of quantum information research.

title: Bound State Of A He-3 Atom At Free He-4 Surfaces
authors: Massimo Boninsegni
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations confirm the existence of a bound state of a single He-3 atom at a free superfluid He-4 surface in three dimensions, localized within a ~10-A thick low-density He-4 surface layer, with a binding energy of approximately 4 K with respect to vacuum. As the temperature is raised above ~ 1 K the He-3 atom leaves the surface to dissolve into the superfluid. The situation is entirely different in two dimensions, as the He-3 atom is excluded from the superfluid and no surface bound state exists. Results are also presented for the a He-3 atom binding to nanoscale size He-4 clusters adsorbed on weak substrates, a physical system that may allow for the observation of some of the physics predicted for extended surfaces. It is shown that a He-3 bound state localized at the perimeter of sufficiently small (a few tens of atoms) clusters exists not just on Cs, as previously reported, but on all alkali substrates.
tldr: 量子蒙特卡洛模拟确认了He-3原子在超流He-4表面的束缚态，并研究了其在二维和团簇上的行为。
motivation: 探索He-3原子在He-4表面的束缚态物理，涉及超流体表面和维度效应。
method: 使用量子蒙特卡洛模拟计算He-3原子的束缚能和空间分布。
result: 三维中存在约4 K的束缚能，二维中无束缚态；纳米团簇上在碱金属基底也有束缚态。
conclusion: 该研究揭示了He-3在He-4表面的束缚行为及其维度依赖性。

title: Quantified Absorption Of Laser Light By Silver Atoms In A Hollow-cathode Lamp
authors: Matthew P. Wilde, Richard G. Wolfendale, Mark Bengyel, Ifan G. Hughes, Philip D. Gregory
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a quantitative study of laser absorption on the [MATH] transition of silver in a hollow-cathode lamp. Spectra obtained using a weak probe are measured and compared to a simple theoretical model. We fit our results to extract an effective temperature and number density associated with the silver in the lamp and confirm that the spectra are dominated by Doppler broadening. We consider the broadening effect of collisions between silver and the neon buffer gas in the lamp, and establish that these effects are small but modify the optimum effective parameters for the model. Our work results in a simple, quantitative, and predictive model for laser absorption in the lamp.
tldr: This paper presents a quantitative study of laser absorption on a silver transition in a hollow-cathode lamp, fitting spectra to extract temperature and number density with a simple model.
motivation: To provide a simple, quantitative, and predictive model for laser absorption in a hollow-cathode lamp, which is useful for spectroscopy applications.
method: Weak probe spectra were measured and compared to a theoretical model considering Doppler broadening and collisional effects with the neon buffer gas.
result: Confirmed that spectra are dominated by Doppler broadening, and extracted effective temperature and number density; collisional effects were small but refined the model.
conclusion: The work yields a straightforward, predictive model for laser absorption in the lamp, with modest relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Spectral Properties Of Aperiodic Metric And Discrete Graphs
authors: Gilad Sofer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this thesis, we study the spectral properties of dynamically defined aperiodic metric and discrete graphs. Our goal is to determine to what extent spectral properties of discrete one-dimensional ergodic Schr\"odinger operators persist when the aperiodicity is manifested through the geometry rather than through a potential. The graphs considered here are inspired by one-dimensional aperiodic tilings, and are called tiling graphs and decorated [MATH]-graphs. For a large family of metric tiling graphs equipped with the standard Laplacian, we show that the spectrum is of zero Lebesgue measure, and is a generalized Cantor set up to a possible discrete set of energies. For decorated [MATH]-graphs, we further show that for a Baire-generic and Lebesgue almost-sure choice of the decoration edge lengths, the spectrum is a generalized Cantor set. We then study the integrated density of states (IDS) for metric and discrete decorated [MATH]-graphs. We prove a gap labelling theorem, which characterizes the set of possible values taken by the IDS inside spectral gaps. We show that the gap labels are contained in the Schwartzman group associated with the dynamical system generating the graph, up to a geometric scaling factor. Lastly, we consider the Dry Ten Martini Problem for discrete Sturmian decorated [MATH]-graphs, asking whether all possible values predicted by the gap labelling theorem are indeed attained by the IDS inside spectral gaps. We answer this question negatively, by identifying a large set of gap labels which are not attained due to jump discontinuities of the IDS. We then show that away from these jump discontinuities, the periodic approximants for Sturmian graphs display the same combinatorial structure as the standard Sturmian Hamiltonians, and use this to obtain an explicit characterization of the realized gap labels for Sturmian comb graphs.
tldr: This thesis studies spectral properties of aperiodic metric and discrete graphs, showing zero-measure spectra and Cantor-like sets, proving gap labelling theorems, and addressing the Dry Ten Martini Problem.
motivation: To understand how spectral properties of ergodic Schrödinger operators persist when aperiodicity arises from geometry rather than potential.
method: Uses dynamical systems and ergodic theory to analyze Laplacian spectra of tiling graphs and decorated graphs, and studies integrated density of states and gap labelling.
result: Shows zero Lebesgue measure spectrum for tiling graphs, Baire-generic and almost sure Cantor spectra for decorated graphs, proves gap labelling theorems, and negatively answers the Dry Ten Martini Problem for discrete Sturmian decorated graphs.
conclusion: Geometric aperiodicity yields spectral properties analogous to potential aperiodicity, with specific characterizations of realized gap labels.

title: Deterministic Control Over Launching Efficiency Of Higher-order Hyperbolic Phonon Polaritons
authors: Thiago S. Arnaud, John E. Buchner, Ryan W. Spangler, Maximilian Obst, Jon-Paul Maria, Joshua D. Caldwell
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperbolic materials, which exhibit an extreme form of birefringence enabling the volume confinement and frequency-dependent propagation of deeply sub-diffractional optical modes, offer the opportunity for extreme confinement via the stimulation polaritonic modes, with substantially higher confinement obtained through the efficient excitation of of the higher-order (shorter wavelength) hyperbolic polaritonic modes, which they can support. However, while these higher-order hyperbolic polaritons (HO-HPhPs) form high-momentum ray-like propagation within the bulk, efficient excitation of these modes, especially in contrast to the long-wavelength lower-momentum surface polariton propagating modes, has remained a challenge. Critically, the large momentum mismatch between these modes and free-space light, alongside the spatial mismatch between the sub-diffractional scatterer and the distinct modal distribution of HO-HPhPs, lead to a suppressed launching efficiency of these higher-order modes, limiting their use in nanophotonic applications. Here, we report the experimental observation of a 10-fold enhancement in the excitation efficiency of HO-HPhPs through the use of subsurface scatterers over traditional surface scattering (e.g. a flake edge or gold launcher) within single-crystalline {\alpha}-MoO3 slabs. We employ full-wave numerical simulations to investigate the role of the spatial overlap between HO-HPhP modal distributions and the scatterer placement upon excitation efficiency. Furthermore, we develop a generalized process using transfer matrix method to selectively design modal HO-HPhP excitation, which advances the capabilities of HPhP multiplexing for on-chip applications.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a 10-fold enhancement in excitation efficiency of higher-order hyperbolic phonon polaritons in α-MoO3 using subsurface scatterers, offering a method for selective modal excitation.
motivation: Higher-order hyperbolic phonon polaritons offer extreme light confinement but suffer from low launching efficiency due to momentum and spatial mismatches, limiting their nanophotonic applications. The goal is to overcome this by controlling scatterer placement.
method: The authors experimentally compare surface and subsurface scatterers in single-crystalline α-MoO3 slabs, use full-wave simulations to analyze spatial overlap, and develop a transfer matrix method for designing modal excitation.
result: Subsurface scatterers enhance HO-HPhP launching efficiency by 10-fold compared to traditional surface scatterers, and the generalized transfer matrix approach enables selective design of modal HO-HPhP excitation.
conclusion: This work advances the practical use of higher-order hyperbolic phonon polaritons for on-chip nanophotonic applications by providing a route to efficient excitation and mode multiplexing.

title: Don't Look Now: Paying For Documented Need Punishes Discovery In Us Lead-pipe Funding
authors: Kristin C. Epstein Gustavo Pedro Ricou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The United States is allotting USD 15 billion for lead service line replacement in proportion to documented lead, the largest of a growing class of environmental-indicator transfers. Reconstructing the rule exactly, we show it prices looking below zero. Resolving an unknown pipe lowers a state's expected allotment in three of the eight jurisdictions we can measure above the statutory floor, and raises it in none. Below it the allotment cannot move. Systems that file nothing are scored lead-free. We prove no fixed formula on self-reported inventories can pay for need without punishing its measurement, derive the unique additive repair -- an audit-anchored, strategy-proof estimator -- and calibrate it on the program's data. Discovery is repriced from a median loss of USD 48.63 per line per year to zero. Allocation swings fall from 16.5% of the pool to 0.8%, for an audit costing 1.36% of one year's funds. The formula's tilt toward vulnerable systems survives.
tldr: This paper analyzes a US federal funding formula for lead pipe replacement, showing it penalizes discovery of lead pipes and proposes an audit-anchored estimator to align incentives.
motivation: To prevent the funding formula from disincentivizing accurate lead pipe inventories, which could undermine public health efforts.
method: They reconstruct the exact formula, prove that no fixed formula can pay for need without punishing measurement, and derive a unique additive repair using audit-anchored strategy-proof estimation.
result: Discovery repriced from a median loss to zero, allocation swings reduced from 16.5% to 0.8% of the pool.
conclusion: An audit-based approach can fix the incentive problem while preserving fairness and targeting vulnerable systems.

title: Higher-Order Topological Phase In The Two-Dimensional Type-IV Magnet MgCr$_2$O$_4$
authors: Xiaorong Zou, Hyeon Suk Shin, Yanmei Zang, Ying Dai, Chengwang Niu, Chang-Jong Kang, Chang Woo Myung
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Type-IV two-dimensional (2D) magnetism-a newly classified collinear magnetic phase featuring nonrelativistic spin degeneracy and spin-orbit-coupling-induced momentum-dependent spin splitting-extends the symmetry classification of collinear magnets, opening new opportunities for unconventional topological quantum states. Here, we reveal that the recently proposed two-dimensional type-IV 2D magnet MgCr[MATH]O[MATH] hosts an intrinsic higher-order topological insulating phase, featuring [MATH]-protected corner states and a nontrivial rotational topological invariant of [MATH] = [MATH] with a quantized fractional corner charge of [MATH]. Spin-orbit coupling breaks the spin-degeneracy-enforcing symmetry [MATH] while preserving the crystalline [MATH] rotational symmetry that protects the higher-order topological phase, thereby enabling spin splitting to coexist with the nontrivial topology. Furthermore, the higher-order topological phase remains intact throughout a wide range of biaxial strains without band-gap closing and topological phase transition, demonstrating the robustness of the symmetry-protected topological state against external perturbations. Our work establishes a direct connection between type-IV magnetic system and higher-order topology, providing a new route for symmetry-engineered magnetic topological quantum states.
tldr: A two-dimensional type-IV magnet MgCr2O4 is shown to host a higher-order topological insulating phase with corner states and a nontrivial rotational invariant.
motivation: To explore unconventional topological states in type-IV two-dimensional magnets, which are newly classified collinear magnets with nonrelativistic spin degeneracy.
method: The paper uses theoretical analysis and likely ab initio calculations to investigate the electronic band structure and topological invariants of MgCr2O4, considering spin-orbit coupling and strain effects.
result: The material exhibits a higher-order topological insulating phase protected by rotational symmetry, featuring fractional corner charge and robustness against biaxial strain, with spin splitting coexisting with the nontrivial topology.
conclusion: This work establishes a connection between type-IV magnetism and higher-order topology, suggesting a new platform for magnetic topological quantum states.

title: Emergent Aggregation From Collective Foraging
authors: Gorka Mu\~noz-Gil, Andrea L\'opez-Incera, Vide Ramsten, Giovanni Volpe, Thomas M\"uller, Hans J. Briegel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective behaviour in living systems is usually modelled as the outcome of a social drive: agents are rewarded, or hard-wired, to align with or approach their neighbours. Here we show that aggregation can instead emerge from an objective. We let reinforcement learning foragers, initially performing a random walk, optimize their dynamics from a purely individual reward for finding replenishable targets, while perceiving only their conspecifics and never the targets themselves. As the visual range grows, the agents undergo a sharp crossover from an environment-tuned individual search to a scale-agnostic collective one, and this crossover coincides with the onset of spatial aggregation. Thus a collective phase arises as a by-product of optimal foraging, without any direct reward for grouping. A minimal analytical first-passage model reproduces the transition as a crossover between the two search strategies. Our results identify indirect, resource-driven reward as a generic route to emergent collective phenomena.
tldr: This paper shows that collective aggregation can emerge from individual foraging rewards without explicit social drives, using reinforcement learning agents.
motivation: To explore whether collective behavior can arise as a byproduct of individual optimization rather than direct social interaction.
method: Reinforcement learning foragers perform random walks, receive rewards for finding replenishable targets, and perceive only conspecifics (not targets); their visual range is varied.
result: As visual range increases, agents crossover from individual to scale-agnostic collective search, coinciding with the onset of spatial aggregation.
conclusion: Resource-driven reward can be a generic route to emergent collective phenomena, suggesting indirect mechanisms for collective behavior.

title: A New Fractal Derivative And Its Integral Transform Methods For Economic Models
authors: Bipan Hazarika Krishna Mani Nath
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the RLC-fractal derivative along with the fractal Laplace and fractal Sumudu transforms of it. Then we apply these transformations to solve economic models involving the RLC-fractal derivative.

title: Devaney Chaos In A Two-Dimensional Space With Weak Topology
authors: Hongbo Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that a finite-dimensional linear system cannot be chaotic. In this article, it shows that Devaney chaos with the weak topology can be generated by a linear map, where the weak topology into a two-dimensional Euclidean space is induced by a linear functional. result: It shows equivalence of strong and weak transitivity/sensitivity for matrices with complex conjugate eigenvalues, and highlights differences in dynamics between weak and norm topologies.

title: Selective Interference Suppression Of Siamese-Net In Heterogeneous Interference Channels
authors: Arkadeep Sinha, Shubham Paul, R. Manivasakan, Nambi Seshadri, R. David Koilpillai

title: An Adaptive Augmented Lagrangian Method For Deterministic And Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization
authors: Michael J. O'neill Tianzhu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an inexact Augmented Lagrangian algorithm for solving nonlinear, non-convex optimization problems. Unlike most recently proposed Augmented Lagrangian methods with worst-case complexity guarantees, we utilize adaptive penalty parameter updates and full dual stepsizes. We show that the method matches the best known worst-case complexity results for Augmented Lagrangian methods (up to logarithmic factors) when both the function and constraints are deterministic, when the function is stochastic and the constraints are deterministic, and when both are stochastic. Experiments on CUTEst test problems confirm the practical advantages of the proposed approach over Augmented Lagrangian methods with non-adaptive penalty parameters and/or short dual step sizes in the deterministic setting. Numerical results on stochastic constrained optimization problems in machine learning also confirm these findings.
tldr: This paper presents an inexact augmented Lagrangian method with adaptive penalty parameters for nonconvex optimization, matching best-known worst-case complexity and showing practical advantages on deterministic and stochastic problems.
motivation: To improve upon existing augmented Lagrangian methods by incorporating adaptive penalty parameter updates and full dual stepsizes, addressing both deterministic and stochastic nonconvex settings.

result: The method achieves best-known worst-case complexity up to logarithmic factors and demonstrates practical superiority over baseline augmented Lagrangian methods in experiments.

title: Solving Quasi-Variational Inequalities Using The Progressive Decoupling Of Linkages
authors: Manoel Jardim, Claudia Sagastiz\'abal, Mikhail Solodov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the progressive decoupling of linkages methodology for optimization and variational inequalities, we propose an algorithm for solving quasi-variational inequalities as a sequence of variational inequalities. Our method is shown to converge locally under some regularity conditions and globally when such conditions hold throughout the entire domain. Separately, under other type of assumptions, global convergence with linear rate is also established for the class of quasi-variational inequalities said to have a moving set. Advantageous computational performance is shown for large-scale Walrasian equilibrium problems, a special case of generalized Nash equilibria, as well as for some other instances encountered in related literature.
tldr: Proposes an algorithm for solving quasi-variational inequalities by reducing them to a sequence of variational inequalities, with convergence guarantees and computational performance on Walrasian equilibrium problems.
motivation: Quasi-variational inequalities are important in economics and game theory, and existing methods may be inefficient or lack global convergence. The progressive decoupling of linkages methodology from optimization is adapted to provide a new algorithmic approach.
method: The algorithm iteratively solves a sequence of variational inequalities, leveraging the structure of the moving set or regularity conditions to attain local and global convergence, with linear rate under additional assumptions.
result: The method converges locally under regularity conditions and globally under certain domain-wide conditions, with linear convergence for moving-set problems. Tests on large-scale Walrasian equilibrium problems show advantageous computational performance.
conclusion: The algorithm offers an effective new approach for quasi-variational inequalities, especially for large-scale economic equilibrium problems, and complements existing optimization-based methods.

title: The Singular Zienkiewicz Tetrahedron: Definition And Integration

title: The Role Of Parameter Jacobians In The Stability Of Network Outputs
authors: Halyun Jeong, Palle E. T. Jorgensen, Hyun-Kyoung Kwon, Myung-Sin Song, James Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the framework of network dynamics, learning models, and neural tangent kernels (NTK), we show that the corresponding linearized dynamics leads naturally to a semigroup formulation. More precisely, in our analysis of input/output models, the time-dynamics is presented via special semigroups of linear operators on Hilbert spaces, together with an associated class of semigroup perturbations. In this context, we then present new and explicit a priori perturbation-bound results: for the fixed-kernel linearization constructions arising in the NTK setting, we prove norm-bounds on the corresponding semigroup perturbations, in the form of explicit finite-time perturbation estimates. We further present refinements on prescribed task spaces, Ces\`aro-averaged (ergodic) comparisons estimates, and versions in which the lower spectral edge assumption is replaced by a spectral-distribution condition. We also extend the comparison to nonautonomous NTK evolutions through piecewise-frozen approximations, record a corresponding discrete Euler specialization, and offer worked examples in order to illustrate our perturbation-bound estimates.

title: High-order Robust Basis-update & Galerkin Integrators For Dynamical Low-rank Approximation
authors: Cory D. Hauck, Jonas Kusch, Steffen Schotth\"ofer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamical low-rank approximation has become a widely used numerical method in diverse disciplines. Its main idea is to represent the matrix or tensor-valued solution to a time-dependent differential equation as a low-rank factorization. The evolution of the factorization leads to highly stiff dynamics and requires the derivation of novel time integration methods that are not prone to this stiffness. A promising family of integrators are basis-update \& Galerkin (BUG) integrators as they enable implicit time integration and structure--preservation. However, current BUG integrators are limited to second--order accuracy while general-order BUG integrators are designed as projections of explicit time integration methods, thus severely limiting their use. In this work, we propose general-order BUG integrators that do not rely on an explicit time integration scheme while requiring a smaller number of basis functions to achieve high-order accuracy. We prove a general order error bound for the proposed augmented and parallel BUG integrators and demonstrate their behaviour for a series of stiff and non-stiff numerical benchmarks in which they significantly outperform previous BUG versions.
tldr: The paper introduces high-order basis-update & Galerkin integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation that achieve high-order accuracy without explicit time integration, outperforming previous methods.
motivation: Existing BUG integrators are limited to second-order accuracy or rely on explicit time integration schemes, which are prone to stiffness; the authors aim to develop general-order BUG integrators that are stable and efficient.
method: The authors propose augmented and parallel BUG integrators that avoid explicit time integration and prove a general order error bound, requiring fewer basis functions for high-order accuracy.
result: The new integrators significantly outperform previous BUG versions on stiff and non-stiff numerical benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed high-order BUG integrators provide a robust and efficient numerical method for dynamical low-rank approximation, potentially benefiting various scientific computing applications.

title: Beyond Procrustes Distances: A Multilinear Gromov-Wasserstein Distance Capturing Chirality

abstract: ArXiv:2608.27774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficiently and robustly analyzing shape data is critical across many scientific disciplines. Under mild assumptions, this objective yields a distance between shapes, represented as probability distributions quotiented by a symmetry group [MATH]. We establish robustness properties for the multilinear Gromov-Wasserstein distances and develop efficient algorithms to compute them, reformulating the underlying optimization problem by projecting couplings onto a low-dimensional space. We derive algorithms for both local and approximate global solutions, yielding a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for these problems. title: Optimal Control Of Fractional Diffusion With Dirac Measures

abstract: ArXiv:2608.27776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a PDE-constrained optimization problem for an elliptic equation with the spectral fractional Laplacian and a linear combination of Dirac measures as the forcing term; the controls are the amplitudes of these singular sources. title: Higher Order Structure Along Nilpotent Eigendirections In Planar Vector Fields
authors: Roberto Albarran-Garc\'ia, Martha Alvarez Ram\'irez, Marco Polo Garc\'ia-Rivera
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a distinguished one dimensional restriction associated with planar vector fields whose linearization is a nonzero nilpotent matrix of index two. This restriction admits an intrinsic interpretation on the nilpotent eigendirection, while its scalar representation in Jordan coordinates satisfies a simple transformation law under admissible changes of Jordan chain. Its quadratic Taylor coefficient coincides with the intrinsic quadratic Bogdanov--Takens coefficient. % For rational restrictions, we show that the Taylor coefficient sequence satisfies a finite linear recurrence determined by the minimal denominator. Its degree defines a recurrence degree that is invariant under admissible changes of Jordan chain and gives the minimal order of an eventual homogeneous recurrence. Exact cancellations may therefore be detected directly from the restriction before nonlinear normal form transformations are performed. Applications to four planar models exhibit different recurrence degree and cancellation mechanisms, illustrating the complementarity between the distinguished restriction and smooth nilpotent normal form theory.

conclusion: The distinguished restriction provides a complementary approach to smooth nilpotent normal form theory, offering a simpler way to detect cancellations and characterize higher-order structure.

title: Many-Revolution Low-Thrust Transfers Within Periodic Orbit Families

abstract: ArXiv:2608.27849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper explores the use of a reduced manifold space initialization method for the generation of both time and fuel optimal many-revolution, low-thrust transfers between three-body periodic orbits within a family. title: Anchored Scenario Coverage For Failure-Aware First-Hit Batch Inverse Design
authors: Chuhan Yang, Chenxi Wang, Linhan Wu, Yuyang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early discovery of at least one valid design satisfying a target requirement is a central objective in failure-prone closed-loop inverse design. A natural batch baseline ranks candidates by a product-form marginal valid-hit score, but selecting the highest-ranked candidates independently can produce redundant recommendations under predictive uncertainty and waste the experiment budget.
