title: A Whole New Side: The Duality Symmetries Of Hitomezashi
authors: Megan A. Martinez
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hitomezashi is a particular style of sashiko stitching characterized by crossing lines of stitches. Certain hitomezashi designs can be encoded with two binary strings and have been the subject of a wide-array of mathematical research. Dubbed generalized hitomezashi patterns (GHPs) by Sen & Martinez, these designs are reversible and can be 'self-dual.' We investigate the possible 'dual-' or 'flip-symmetries' in GHPs; the inclusion of these symmetries is equivalent to considering two-colour symmetry groups. Following the work of Sen & Martinez, who found the wallpaper symmetry groups that are compatible with GHPs, this paper investigates the possible two-colour symmetries compatible with GHPs. We prove that there are four possible rosette two-colour symmetry types, completely describe the properties on binary strings that create these symmetries, and prove that exactly 17 of the 46 two-colour wallpaper groups are compatible with GHPs.
tldr: The paper classifies the two-colour symmetry groups of generalized hitomezashi patterns, showing that exactly 17 of 46 possible wallpaper groups are compatible.
motivation: Investigate the dual or flip symmetries in hitomezashi patterns, which are encoded by binary strings, to understand their symmetry properties.
method: Uses group theory to analyze the compatibility of two-colour symmetry groups with generalized hitomezashi patterns.
result: Proves that there are four possible rosette two-colour symmetry types and that exactly 17 of the 46 two-colour wallpaper groups are compatible with GHPs.
conclusion: Provides a complete classification of the possible two-colour symmetries in hitomezashi patterns, extending prior work on wallpaper groups.

title: Infinitely Many Graph Manifolds With Unique Geometrical Piece That Admit Arbitrarily Many Anosov Flows
authors: V. Shmukler O. Pochinka
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anosov flows have a long and rich history, firstly motivated by the study of geodesic flows in negative curvature surface by Anosov and Sinai. Not every closed manifold admits an Anosov flow for well-known reasons: the fundamental group of a 3-manifold \(M\) admitting an Anosov flow must have exponential growth, and \(M\) must be universally covered by \(^{3}\). Nevertheless, there are sufficient mechanisms for constructing distinct Anosov flows on admissible 3-manifolds, such as Dehn-Goodman-Fried surgery or playing with hyperbolic building blocks. A central problem in the field has been to determine the number of Anosov flows that can be supported by a single manifold. The question of whether there exists an infinite set of pairwise non-equivalent Anosov flows on a 3-manifold remains open to this day. However, there are several papers proving the existence of a manifold [MATH] that admits [MATH] pairwise inequivalent Anosov flows for any natural number [MATH]. In all known examples, the manifolds [MATH] are composed of several geometric pieces. In the present paper, we prove the existence of a countable number of graph manifolds [MATH], [MATH] with a single geometric piece, each of which admits [MATH] pairwise non-equivalent transitive Anosov flows. All previously known constructions of different flows on the same graph manifold were based on gluing geodesic flows. The nature of the flows constructed in this paper is completely different; they are constructed from a single hyperbolic plug, which is a suspension over a Morse-Smale diffeomorphism on a surface.
tldr: This paper constructs infinitely many graph manifolds with a single geometric piece that admit arbitrarily many non-equivalent transitive Anosov flows, using a hyperbolic plug.
motivation: The central problem is to determine the number of Anosov flows a single 3-manifold can support, and previously known constructions required multiple geometric pieces.
method: The authors construct the flows from a single hyperbolic plug, which is a suspension over a Morse-Smale diffeomorphism on a surface, instead of gluing geodesic flows.
result: They prove the existence of a countable number of graph manifolds with a single geometric piece, each admitting arbitrarily many pairwise non-equivalent transitive Anosov flows.
conclusion: This provides a completely new construction mechanism for Anosov flows on graph manifolds, differing from all prior approaches.

title: Solution Methods For Infinite-Dimensional Generalized Disjunctive Programming
authors: Joshua L. Pulsipher Daniel Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) expresses mixed discrete-continuous decisions through Boolean indicators and disjunctions, and can be systematically solved via a library of methods proposed in the literature. The recent InfiniteGDP abstraction lifts this modeling layer to continuous domains such as time, space, and uncertainty, but only the big-M and hull reformulations, the two endpoints of the relaxation spectrum, have been generalized to the infinite setting. This work closes this gap by generalizing four other GDP solution methods to infinite-dimensional optimization: the multiple big-M reformulation, P-split reformulation, cutting plane reformulation, and the logic-based outer approximation algorithm. It further proposes MBM-GP, a novel Gaussian-process variant of multiple big-M that learns the big-M function over the infinite domain from a small subset of the subproblem solves. Moreover, these approaches are implemented in the Julia package InfiniteDisjunctiveProgramming.jl. The methods are benchmarked on case studies arising in dynamic and stochastic optimization. The results demonstrate how the generalized solution methods can outperform big-M and hull, with MBM-GP retaining the tightness of multiple big-M at a fraction of its reformulation cost.
tldr: The paper develops solution methods for infinite-dimensional generalized disjunctive programming, a mathematical optimization problem, with no connection to quantum information or related fields.
motivation: To extend GDP solution methods from finite to infinite-dimensional settings such as time, space, and uncertainty, which are not covered by existing approaches.
method: Generalizes four GDP solution methods (multiple big-M, P-split, cutting plane, logic-based outer approximation) to infinite dimensions and proposes MBM-GP, a Gaussian-process variant that learns the big-M function from a subset of subproblem solves.
result: The generalized methods outperform the existing big-M and hull reformulations on case studies, with MBM-GP achieving comparable tightness to multiple big-M at lower computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed methods are effective and implemented in a Julia package, offering practical tools for infinite-dimensional GDP problems.

title: On Lipschitz Spaces, Semigroup Transference, And Heat Kernel Derivative Estimates In Dunkl--Schr\"odinger Analysis
authors: Agnieszka Hejna-{\l}y\.zwa
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study Lipschitz spaces adapted to Dunkl--Schr\"odinger operators [MATH], where [MATH] is the Dunkl Laplacian and [MATH] belongs to the reverse H\"older class [MATH] with [MATH]. For [MATH], we establish the full equivalence between the heat semigroup-based Lipschitz spaces [MATH] and the pointwise weighted Zygmund classes [MATH] defined via the critical radius function [MATH]. Remarkably, this characterization shows that the spatial smoothness component decouples completely from the underlying reflection group symmetries and root systems. As an intermediate result, we establish new equivalences for inhomogeneous weighted Lipschitz spaces associated with the unperturbed Dunkl Laplacian [MATH]. A central difficulty in this context --- arising from the necessity to disentangle the Euclidean distance from the orbit metric [MATH] --- is resolved through a detailed geometric analysis. Finally, we provide pointwise Gaussian upper bounds for the time derivatives of the Dunkl--Schr\"odinger heat kernel, which are of independent interest for future work in harmonic analysis on Dunkl structures. Crucially, we do not assume the potential [MATH] to be [MATH]-invariant under the action of the Weyl group, which introduces major geometric difficulties resolved here via a local analysis of the orbit metric.
tldr: A pure mathematics paper studying Lipschitz spaces and heat kernel estimates for Dunkl--Schrödinger operators.
motivation: To characterize spatial smoothness in the context of Dunkl--Schrödinger operators and prove pointwise bounds for heat kernel derivatives.
method: Uses heat semigroup theory, weighted Zygmund classes, and geometric analysis of the orbit metric.
result: Establishes equivalence between heat semigroup-based Lipschitz spaces and weighted Zygmund classes, and proves Gaussian upper bounds for time derivatives of the heat kernel.
conclusion: The work advances harmonic analysis on Dunkl structures but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Below-threshold Bistability And Implementation Lag In A Simplex Model Of Radical Vote-Share Dynamics
authors: Alexander Omelchenko
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a nonautonomous compartmental model on the probability simplex for radical vote-share dynamics under delayed policy implementation. The model distinguishes a target regime from an effective regime that adjusts with finite speed and includes a persistent alienation reservoir that can later be mobilised by radical actors. In a symmetric benchmark, persistent alienation destroys the global one-threshold picture: below the local instability threshold, a radical-free centrist--alienated equilibrium may coexist with a stable positive equilibrium, separated by a saddle branch created in a saddle-node bifurcation. By hyperbolic persistence, this coexistence survives near the symmetric baseline, while numerical exploration identifies a wider bistable region under asymmetric perturbations. Delayed implementation further separates target and effective threshold passage, producing a parameter-space lag and an additional state-space lag before a visible response in radical support. The analysis combines a Perron--Frobenius threshold for the frozen radical-free equilibrium, a geometric characterisation of positive equilibria, local adiabatic tracking under slow uniformly subcritical drift, and explicit delay bounds for transversal threshold passage. Under initial matching, the parameter-space delay scales as \(O(\kappa_\theta^{-1})\); in a monotone ramp example the bound is nearly attained, whereas the state-space lag is substantially larger and less sensitive to implementation speed. Thus threshold restoration is preventive rather than curative: once the trajectory enters the basin of the radicalised attractor, returning below the local threshold need not restore the radical-free regime.
tldr: This paper analyzes a compartmental model of radical vote-share dynamics with delayed policy implementation, revealing bistability and implementation lags.
motivation: To understand the impact of delayed policy implementation on radical vote-share dynamics and threshold behavior.
method: Uses a nonautonomous compartmental model on the probability simplex, with Perron-Frobenius threshold analysis, saddle-node bifurcation, adiabatic tracking, and delay bounds.
result: Persistent alienation leads to bistability below the threshold, and delayed implementation introduces parameter-space and state-space lags scaling as O(kappa_theta^{-1}), with the state-space lag being larger.
conclusion: Threshold restoration is preventive rather than curative; returning below the threshold does not guarantee recovery from a radicalized regime.

title: A Massively Parallel Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Solver For Direct Numerical Simulation Of Compressible Flows On GPUs
authors: Andrew Welter, Thea Collin, Ngoc Cuong Nguyen, Jaime Peraire
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct numerical simulation (DNS) of compressible transitional and turbulent flows requires numerical methods that combine high-order accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency to resolve a broad range of spatial and temporal scales. This paper presents a massively parallel hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) solver for DNS of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations on GPU-accelerated high-performance computing systems. The proposed solver combines high-order HDG discretization with robust shock capturing, diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta (DIRK) time integration, and an efficient Newton-GMRES solution strategy accelerated by additive Schwarz preconditioning and reduced-basis approximation. A distributed implementation of these methods based on GPU-aware MPI, Kokkos, and CUDA/HIP libraries enables scalable execution on heterogeneous computing platforms. The solver is demonstrated on three canonical benchmark problems covering a wide range of Mach-number flow regimes: subsonic transitional flow over the Eppler 387 airfoil, the supersonic Taylor-Green vortex, and hypersonic boundary-layer transition. Numerical results are compared with available experimental measurements and published DNS data, showing good agreement across distinct flow regimes. The results demonstrate the ability of the proposed solver to resolve laminar-turbulent transition, strong compressibility effects, shock-associated flow structures, and fully three-dimensional turbulent dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated solver for direct numerical simulation of compressible flows using a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method.
motivation: To enable high-fidelity simulation of transitional and turbulent compressible flows with high-order accuracy and computational efficiency.
method: Combines HDG discretization with shock capturing, DIRK time integration, Newton-GMRES solver with additive Schwarz preconditioning, and GPU-accelerated parallel implementation.
result: Demonstrated on airfoil, Taylor-Green vortex, and hypersonic boundary-layer transition, showing good agreement with experiments and published DNS data.
conclusion: The solver is effective for resolving complex compressible flow phenomena, but it is not related to quantum information or thermodynamic research.

title: Optimal Error Estimates For The Half-way Bounce-back Lattice Boltzmann Method For The Stokes Equations
authors: Kai Koike
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a mathematical proof of the optimal convergence rates for the D2Q9 BGK lattice Boltzmann method with the half-way bounce-back rule for the incompressible Stokes equations in a flat channel. The convergence rates are second-order for the velocity and first-order for the pressure as the lattice spacing [MATH] tends to zero, in agreement with formal analyses and numerical experiments, whereas the available rigorous convergence theorems only yield an [MATH] bound for the velocity error. A key step in the proof is a decomposition of the leading boundary consistency error into macroscopic and kinetic components. These components are absorbed by suitably constructed Stokes and discrete Knudsen layer correctors, respectively. Incorporating these correctors into the prediction function used in previous rigorous analyses, we obtain a refined prediction function with consistency errors of sufficiently high order. Combined with the known weighted [MATH]-stability estimate, this gives the optimal convergence rates.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous proof that the D2Q9 BGK lattice Boltzmann method with half-way bounce-back achieves optimal second-order velocity and first-order pressure convergence for Stokes equations in a flat channel.
motivation: Previous rigorous analyses only yielded suboptimal error bounds, while numerical experiments suggested higher order. The paper aims to close this gap by proving optimal convergence rates.
method: By decomposing the boundary consistency error into macroscopic and kinetic components and constructing Stokes and discrete Knudsen layer correctors, the authors refine the prediction function to achieve high-order consistency, combined with a weighted stability estimate.
result: The proof establishes second-order convergence for velocity and first-order for pressure, matching numerical observations.
conclusion: The optimal error estimates are now rigorously proven, confirming the expected accuracy of the lattice Boltzmann method for Stokes flow.

title: A Two-Level Preconditioner Based On Dominant Components For Time-Dependent Multiscale High-Contrast Problem
authors: Yating Wang, Yibao Li, Wing Tat Leung
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a two-level overlapping preconditioner for time-dependent problems in high-contrast multiscale media. We present a coarse-space construction based on multiscale methods, with emphasis on the relaxed nonlocal multicontinuum (NLMC) method. The NLMC space can be separated into components representing the high-permeability regions and the low-permeability background. We show that the complete NLMC space effectively preconditions the heterogeneous stiffness operator, whereas the high-permeability component alone captures the contrast-dependent global modes. For suitable small time-step sizes, the mass matrix controls the low-permeability contribution and only the high-permeability component in NLMC space is required for the global coarse correction in the two-level preconditioner. For general time-step sizes, performance can be maintained by using the full NLMC space or augmenting the high-permeability component with a standard multiscale space. The proposed coarse-space construction lowers the computational cost while preserving robustness with respect to coefficient contrast and fine-scale resolution. To further improve efficiency, the multiscale basis functions can be constructed by iteratively solving the relaxed energy-minimizing formulation. We demonstrate the robustness, efficiency and scalability of the proposed method through several numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper develops a two-level overlapping preconditioner for time-dependent multiscale high-contrast problems using the relaxed nonlocal multicontinuum method.
motivation: To efficiently solve time-dependent problems in multiscale media with high contrast coefficients, where standard preconditioners fail due to contrast-dependent global modes.
method: The authors construct a coarse space based on the NLMC method, separating components for high-permeability regions and low-permeability background, and use either the full NLMC space or augment the high-permeability component with a standard multiscale space depending on time-step size.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate robustness, efficiency, and scalability, with lower computational cost while preserving contrast and resolution robustness.
conclusion: The proposed coarse-space construction offers a computationally efficient preconditioner for time-dependent multiscale high-contrast problems, adaptable to different time-step sizes.

title: On Solving Continuous-Discrete Projection Filters Via Sum-of-Squares Relaxation
authors: Muhammad F. Emzir
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The continuous-discrete projection filter offers a rigorous framework to approximate the solution of the nonlinear state estimation problems. However, it suffers from numerical instability during the prediction phase when integration errors force the natural parameters outside their admissible domain. To address this issue, we introduce the sum-of-squares (SOS) relaxation to constrain the evolution of the natural parameters within the admissible domain. By parameterizing the underlying SOS matrix using the log-Cholesky map, we derive a projected ordinary differential equation (ODE) that inherently preserves the necessary positivity constraints without requiring the computationally expensive online optimization checks associated with previous semi-infinite programming approach. We provide a theoretical derivation of this positivity-preserving propagation scheme and present the explicit SOS-relaxed evolution equations for the Gaussian case.
tldr: This paper introduces a sum-of-squares relaxation to constrain the evolution of natural parameters in continuous-discrete projection filters, addressing numerical instability during prediction.
motivation: The continuous-discrete projection filter suffers from numerical instability when integration errors force natural parameters outside their admissible domain.
method: The authors use sum-of-squares relaxation with log-Cholesky parameterization to derive a projected ODE that preserves positivity constraints without expensive online optimization.
result: They provide a theoretical derivation and explicit SOS-relaxed evolution equations for the Gaussian case.
conclusion: The proposed method inherently preserves positivity while avoiding computationally expensive online checks, improving stability of the filter.

title: Invariant Sphere Theorem And Ring-Coupled Systems
authors: Pedro Soares
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we show how heteroclinic networks can arise in a simple class of network dynamical systems through the application of the Invariant Sphere Theorem. Ring-coupled systems are ODE networks in [MATH] in which each variable [MATH] interacts only with its predecessor [MATH]. We derive conditions on the coefficients of a cubic polynomial that guarantee the existence of a globally attracting invariant sphere via the Invariant Sphere Theorem. Moreover, setting one of these coefficients to zero, we identify conditions on the remaining coefficients that guarantee the existence of a heteroclinic network on the invariant sphere. Focusing on the case [MATH], we investigate perturbations of the vanishing coefficient in a neighbourhood of the heteroclinic network. Under such perturbations, the heteroclinic network is destroyed and periodic orbits emerge. When the original heteroclinic network is asymptotically stable, the resulting periodic orbits shadow the network. In one parameter regime, a unique attracting periodic orbit appears and shadows the entire heteroclinic network. By contrast, when the heteroclinic network is not stable, repelling periodic orbits arise that shadow only part of the heteroclinic structure, namely half of the heteroclinic connections. Symmetry plays a fundamental role throughout the analysis. Exploiting the symmetries of the system, we reduce the heteroclinic network to two homoclinic orbits. Furthermore, the local dynamics near the heteroclinic network can be studied on a quotient space consisting of an annulus attached to a M\"obius band, with each homoclinic orbit lying on one of these components. This reduction provides a geometric framework for understanding the bifurcations and the emergence of the periodic dynamics.
tldr: This paper studies heteroclinic networks in ring-coupled dynamical systems using the Invariant Sphere Theorem and analyzes perturbations that lead to periodic orbits.
motivation: To understand how heteroclinic networks can emerge in simple network dynamical systems and the dynamics near them.
method: Derives conditions on cubic polynomial coefficients for a globally attracting invariant sphere, then identifies heteroclinic network existence, and reduces the system via symmetry to analyze local dynamics.
result: Conditions for heteroclinic network existence are found; perturbations of a coefficient destroy the network and create periodic orbits that either shadow the entire network (if stable) or only part of it (if unstable).
conclusion: Symmetry reduction provides a geometric framework for understanding bifurcations and the emergence of periodic dynamics in ring-coupled systems.

title: Rope: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement Against Indirect Prompt Injection
authors: Xinhang Ma, Chaowei Xiao, William Yeoh, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) plants instructions in the content a tool-using LLM agent reads, steering the agent into harmful tool calls. The strongest defenses are system-level, leveraging techniques such as task-conditional tool screening to prevent execution of malicious tools, and information-flow control to avoid tool execution with untrusted parameters. However, as agents grow more capable, users delegate more to automation. Consequently, tool execution sequences and parameter values are increasingly determined at runtime and cannot be reliably screened from solely user's query without significant utility loss. We present ROPE (Routed Origin Policy Enforcement), which is anchored in a structural notion of trust: a value may reach a state-changing tool only if it traces unforgeably to the user, a source the user explicitly named, or the user's own authoritative records. Enforcement is then a deterministic origin check over an audited set of sensitive tool parameters, and the only reliance on a language model involves solely the trusted user request, out of the attacker's reach. Our approach admits two provable guarantees: 1) at every step of a trajectory, no value whose only origin is attacker-writable content reaches an origin-guarded parameter, and 2) no rewording of an injection changes an admission decision. We evaluate across four agent models on open-ended agent suites, ROPE holds attack success rate to 1.6--2.6\% while retaining 82--100\% of undefended clean utility, significantly exceeding state-of-the-art system-level defenses in utility while attaining comparable or better security. Further, we show that optimizing the injection against ROPE is largely ineffective, while long-horizon attacks that defeat prior system-level defenses achieve zero success rate. Our code and logs are available at [URL] .
tldr: ROPE is a system-level defense against indirect prompt injection attacks on LLM agents, using a deterministic origin check to ensure sensitive tool parameters only trace to trusted sources.
motivation: Indirect prompt injection attacks can steer tool-using LLM agents into harmful actions, and existing system-level defenses suffer utility loss as agents become more autonomous.
method: ROPE enforces a structural trust model where a value may reach a state-changing tool only if it origins from the user, explicitly named sources, or user's authoritative records; it performs deterministic origin checks on audited sensitive parameters, with LLM reliance limited to the trusted user request.
result: Across four agent models, ROPE reduces attack success rate to 1.6-2.6% while retaining 82-100% of undefended clean utility, outperforming state-of-the-art defenses in utility with comparable or better security.
conclusion: ROPE provides provable security guarantees against indirect prompt injection with minimal utility loss, and optimizing injections against it is largely ineffective.

title: Fully Unleashing The Multimodal Attacker: Meta-Adaptive Jailbreaking Of Vision-Language Models
authors: Benlei Cui, Shen Pang, Yuke Wang, Xuemei Dong, Yuwen Zhai, Jingqun Tang, Haiyang Yu, Hui Xue, Longtao Huang, Haiwen Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The safety of large vision-language models is increasingly stress-tested by multimodal jailbreaks, yet existing attacks remain largely static at the meta level: template-based attacks freeze the image--text layout, while iterative attacks adapt only the image--text content with fixed attack strategies and frozen attacker parameters. We propose Meta-Adaptive Multimodal Jailbreaking (MAMJ), which instead optimizes the attacker itself along two axes: an attack strategy prompt (ASP) [MATH] governing attack iteration and attacker weights [MATH] determining attack effectiveness. Across groups of multimodal attack trajectories, an LLM-based critique first refines [MATH], after which group-aggregated attack-success-rate (ASR) rewards update [MATH]. On MM-SafetyBench, MAMJ achieves [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] ASR against GPT-4o, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, and Seed 2.0, respectively, outperforming the strongest sample-level baseline by up to [MATH] percentage points. The learned attacker [MATH] also transfers without retraining to unseen victims and remains effective under representative defenses. These results reveal a systemic vulnerability of frontier VLMs to meta-adaptive jailbreaks and motivate defenses against meta-level adversaries. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a meta-adaptive jailbreaking method for vision-language models, optimizing attack strategies and weights to improve attack success rate across different models.
motivation: Existing multimodal jailbreaks are static or only adapt content, not the attack strategy itself; this work aims to optimize the attacker at a meta level to achieve higher success rates.
method: The method uses an LLM-based critique to refine an attack strategy prompt and group-aggregated attack success rate rewards to update attacker weights, iteratively optimizing the attacker.
result: On MM-SafetyBench, the method achieves high ASR against several frontier VLMs, outperforming sample-level baselines and transferring to unseen victims.
conclusion: This reveals a systemic vulnerability of frontier VLMs to meta-adaptive jailbreaks and motivates defense against meta-level adversaries.

title: Refundable Deposits: How To Restore Cooperation In Finitely Repeated Games
authors: Giulio Salizzoni, Domenico Mergoni Cecchelli, Edward Plumb, Maryam Kamgarpour, Galit Ashkenazi-Golan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While infinitely repeated games admit a rich set of Nash equilibria, finitely repeated games typically have a much smaller and often inefficient one. We show how to enlarge this set using deposits: in each period a player may place a refundable sum with a neutral intermediary, returned when the game ends and forfeited following a deviation. Paying these deposits is voluntary and incentive compatible at every stage, so no commitment by the players is assumed, the only commitment required being that of the intermediary to a refund rule fixed before play begins. The mechanism sustains payoff profiles more efficient than those of the standard equilibria, without altering the underlying game and without transfers between players. We demonstrate it on the prisoner's dilemma, a congestion game, and a public goods game, all settings where cooperation cannot emerge in the standard finitely repeated version. We also apply it to a dynamic common-pool resource, suggesting that the construction extends beyond repeated stage-games.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism using voluntary refundable deposits with a neutral intermediary to restore cooperation in finitely repeated games.
motivation: Finitely repeated games typically have inefficient equilibria, and the paper aims to enlarge the set of achievable outcomes to support cooperation.
method: The mechanism introduces refundable deposits: each period a player can place a sum with an intermediary, which is returned at the end if no deviation occurs, and forfeited otherwise; deposits are voluntary and incentive compatible at every stage.
result: The mechanism sustains more efficient payoff profiles and is demonstrated on the prisoner's dilemma, a congestion game, a public goods game, and a dynamic common-pool resource.
conclusion: Refundable deposits can restore cooperation without altering the underlying game or requiring player commitment, potentially extending beyond repeated stage-games.

title: Approval-Based Apportionment: Like Portioning, Approximately Like Committee Voting
authors: Hannane Yaghoubizade Paul G\"olz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study approval-based apportionment, a variant of committee elections in which candidates ("parties") can be selected several times. We show that the proportionality axioms EJR, EJR+, and FJR coincide, and so do PJR, PJR+, and FPJR; that Lindahl priceability, an axiom implying core stability, is equivalent to a notion of approximate optimality with respect to the proportional approval voting (PAV) score; and that locally PAV-optimal committees are priceable. Approval-based apportionment (where a candidate receives an integer number of seats) lies between committee elections (zero or one seat) and portioning (a fractional number of seats). We formally connect portioning and apportionment by giving a construction that lifts axioms from apportionment to portioning and preserves implications between them. Several of our new implications between apportionment axioms are natural from a portioning perspective, leading us to believe that apportionment sits closer to portioning than to committee elections. None of them holds in committee elections, but several extend approximately, which makes apportionment a fruitful setting for conjecturing approximate relationships in approval-based committee elections.
tldr: This paper studies approval-based apportionment, showing equivalences among proportionality axioms and establishing connections to portioning.
motivation: To understand the theoretical properties of approval-based apportionment and its relationship to committee voting and portioning.
method: The paper provides formal proofs of axiom equivalences and constructs a lifting from apportionment to portioning that preserves implications.
result: It shows that EJR, EJR+, and FJR coincide, and that Lindahl priceability is equivalent to a notion of approximate optimality for PAV, with local PAV-optimal committees being priceable.
conclusion: Apportionment is closer to portioning than to committee elections, and it serves as a fruitful setting for conjecturing approximate relationships in approval-based committee elections.

title: Condorcet-Winning Sets And Peer Selection In Planar Metric Elections
authors: Ulysse Hennebelle Gabriel de Azevedo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In ranked-choice voting, a Condorcet-winning set is a group of candidates for which no outside candidate is preferred to every member of the group by a majority of voters. We study Condorcet-winning sets in planar metric elections, where voters rank candidates according to their distance under a given norm. We formulate general metric elections, peer selection, and the one-round Voronoi game as instances of a two-player Stackelberg game and place these problems in a common hierarchy. We also introduce a new variant, which we call strong peer selection. Our main result concerns peer selection under the [MATH] and [MATH] norms. We prove that every planar instance admits a Condorcet-winning set of size at most three, even under strong peer selection. This follows from a new result for strong rectangular [MATH]-nets. We show that, for every set of points in the plane, one can choose at most three input points that intersect every axis-parallel rectangle containing more than half of the points, improving the previous threshold of [MATH] due to Ashok et al. Under the [MATH] norm, we prove that every planar metric election admits a Condorcet-winning set of size at most four, improving on the general bound of five due to Song et al. Finally, we give new norm-independent bounds for the one-round Voronoi game.
tldr: This paper studies Condorcet-winning sets in planar metric elections, proving bounds on the size of such sets under different norms, and connects to peer selection and Voronoi games.
motivation: To understand when a small group of candidates can be preferred by a majority over any outside candidate in ranked-choice voting with geometric preferences.
method: Uses combinatorial geometry and game-theoretic analysis, introducing strong peer selection and improving results on strong rectangular nets.
result: Shows that every planar instance admits a Condorcet-winning set of size at most three under L1 and L∞ norms (even with strong peer selection), and at most four under L2 norm, improving previous bounds.
conclusion: Provides new norm-independent bounds for the one-round Voronoi game and places these problems in a common hierarchy.

title: Semantic Watermarking With Order-Robust Detection Over Sub-sentence Units
authors: Abdulrahman Diaa, Jonathan Petit, Florian Kerschbaum
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic watermarks tie the mark to sentence meaning rather than token choices, promising robustness to content-preserving edits. However, the detector only observes attacker-supplied text, which can be reworded, reordered, or resegmented to evade detection without content loss. Rewording, reordering, and resegmentation all cause embedding displacement: detection tests embeddings different from those selected during watermarking and can therefore lose the mark. Our adaptive embedding displacement attack (EDA) admits all three edits under a single objective that maximizes this displacement. It uses a public paraphraser and surrogate encoder without access to the provider's generator or secret key. At a 5% false-positive rate (FPR) and content-preservation threshold [MATH], EDA successfully removes the mark on between 32.6% and 47.9% of documents across four schemes, the highest among the tested attacks. Therefore, EDA evaluates the schemes' robustness more thoroughly than passive paraphrasing. To address these vulnerabilities, we design (k)-SwordStamp: semantic watermarks with order-robust detection over sub-sentence units, reducing sensitivity to attacker-chosen structure at a small quality cost. Against k-SwordStamp, the strongest no-box attack we test is an EDA variant adapted to its design, with a 10.8% attack-success rate. A stronger EDA with access to the provider's detector and secret key reaches a 39.7% attack-success rate, compared with 65.5% on k-SemStamp. Our code is available at [URL].
tldr: The paper introduces an adaptive embedding displacement attack (EDA) against semantic watermarks and proposes k-SwordStamp, a robust watermarking scheme with order-robust detection over sub-sentence units.
motivation: Semantic watermarks are vulnerable to content-preserving edits (rewording, reordering, resegmentation) that cause embedding displacement, allowing attackers to evade detection. Existing defenses like passive paraphrasing are insufficient.
method: They design an adaptive embedding displacement attack (EDA) that unifies all three edit types under a single objective to maximize displacement, using a public paraphraser and surrogate encoder. They also design k-SwordStamp, which uses order-robust detection over sub-sentence units to reduce sensitivity to attacker-chosen structure.
result: EDA removes the mark on 32.6%–47.9% of documents across four schemes at 5% false-positive rate, outperforming passive paraphrasing. Against k-SwordStamp, EDA success rate drops to 10.8% (no-box) and 39.7% with access to detector and key, vs 65.5% against k-SemStamp.
conclusion: k-SwordStamp significantly improves robustness against content-preserving attacks while incurring small quality cost, demonstrating the effectiveness of order-robust detection over sub-sentence units.

title: Revisiting Continuous Noise Sampling For Multi-Party Differential Privacy
authors: Tianhao Wang Yucheng Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combining secure multi-party computation (MPC) with differential privacy (DP) enables multiple parties to release aggregate statistics without a trusted curator, and the core primitive is the protocol to sample noise from a continuous distribution under finite-precision arithmetic. In this paper, we revisit the continuous noise sampling protocols and present several improvements in both security and efficiency. We start by identifying a vulnerability in widely used sample-and-scale constructions. We demonstrate that the scaling operation in arithmetic circuits confines the noise to a sparse, publicly known set of values, so that an adversary can observe the released noisy queries and decide which dataset produced them. As concrete demonstrations, we instantiate attacks on two systems employing such ``flawed'' sampling protocols: Orchard (OSDI'20) for DP secure aggregation and DP-BREM[MATH] (USENIX Sec'25) for DP federated learning. We report a near-[MATH] attack success rate on both systems, under any noise scaler [MATH] used in practice. The leakage we reveal is intrinsic to the scaling operation, and direct repairs either substantially sacrifice utility or add significant precision bits to make the sampling more expensive. To address the security and efficiency issues together, we turn to discrete sampling at the granularity of individual biased bits. We make several optimizations to the sampler and prove its security. Our implementation achieves [MATH] speedup over existing secure discrete samplers and orders-of-magnitude speedup over the insecure sample-and-scale paradigm, with negligible utility loss compared to the ideal continuous mechanism.
tldr: This paper identifies a vulnerability in continuous noise sampling protocols for multi-party differential privacy and proposes efficient discrete sampling optimizations.
motivation: Combining secure multi-party computation with differential privacy requires sampling continuous noise under finite-precision arithmetic, but existing sample-and-scale constructions have a security flaw that leaks information.
method: The authors demonstrate attacks on two systems using flawed sample-and-scale protocols, then propose and prove the security of optimized discrete sampling at the granularity of individual biased bits.
result: The optimized sampler achieves significant speedup over existing secure discrete samplers and orders-of-magnitude speedup over the insecure sample-and-scale paradigm, with negligible utility loss.
conclusion: The proposed discrete sampling approach simultaneously improves both security and efficiency for continuous noise sampling in multi-party differential privacy.

title: GraftyVul: Synthesising Insecure Programs Through Real-World Vulnerability Grafting
authors: Omri Ram, Mitchell Horner, Ron van der Meyden, Alsharif Abuadbba, Hammond Pearce
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vulnerability datasets underpin a wide range of security research, including vulnerability detection, automated remediation, and secure code generation. However, existing datasets sacrifice at least one of three desirable properties: diversity (of language or vulnerability type), reproducibility/executability, or realism. We therefore present GraftyVul, a system that constructs vulnerable programs by grafting real-world vulnerabilities into open-source projects. This grounds the dataset in vulnerabilities observed in real-world contexts while harnessing known good build and test environments, enabling exploit-verification scripts to guarantee that an introduced vulnerability successfully alters a program's behaviour. Using GraftyVul, we generate 212 verified and exploitable vulnerable programs spanning five programming languages (Python, TypeScript, Java, Go, and C#) across 23 CWE categories. To evaluate fidelity, we introduce a language- and context-agnostic semantic embedding that compares vulnerabilities by sink, mechanism and host-feature rather than surface code. This approach outperforms standard code embeddings on cross-language clone and CWE classification. These embeddings demonstrate that GraftyVul samples retain a strong semantic signature to their source vulnerability. We additionally compare GraftyVul against 13 widely used datasets, where it attains competitive diversity while being the only reproducible-exploit dataset with broad language and CWE coverage. Finally, we illustrate GraftyVul's practical utility through an industrial case study evaluating a production vulnerability remediation system.
tldr: GraftyVul generates verified vulnerable programs by grafting real-world vulnerabilities into open-source projects, producing a diverse and reproducible vulnerability dataset across multiple languages and CWE categories.
motivation: Existing vulnerability datasets sacrifice diversity, reproducibility/executability, or realism; the authors aim to create a dataset that has all three.
method: They graft real-world vulnerabilities into open-source projects, use build/test environments to verify exploitability, and introduce a semantic embedding to compare vulnerabilities.
result: They generate 212 verified exploitable programs across 5 languages and 23 CWE categories, and their embeddings outperform standard code embeddings on cross-language clone and CWE classification.
conclusion: GraftyVul is a practical tool for generating realistic and reproducible vulnerability datasets, demonstrated through an industrial case study.

title: Not To Break, But To Attest: Adversarial Probes For Privacy-Preserving Llm Verification
authors: Cameron Wilding, Mina Shaker, Fatemeh Ganji
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-deployment changes to large language models can alter behavior while leaving routine outputs largely unchanged, creating a challenge for AI governance when model weights are proprietary. We present a privacy-preserving zk-SNARK-based audit framework that searches for probes designed in the spirit of adversarial examples to amplify logit drift between an approved model and a modified deployment. Our framework explores complementary probe families under different access models. Token-based probes operate in a black-box setting and require only the input interface, tokenizer, and vocabulary. Embedding-based probes require gray-box access to the embedding interface. Stress probes rely on additional interface capabilities but do not require full white-box access to model weights or architecture. This range allows probe selection to balance sensitivity, access requirements, and deployment cost. We evaluate probe constructions across LLM architectures, model-tampering scenarios representative of post-deployment attacks, and GPU platforms. Importantly, our experimental results demonstrate that token-based probes consistently deliver the strongest mean sensitivity across models and GPU platforms, although operating in a black-box setting. Our Groth16 zk-SNARK workflow remains practical as the probe set scales from 1 to 50, where proving time increases from 1.02 to 1.78 seconds, verification remains near 0.84 seconds, and proof size remains constant.
tldr: This paper presents a privacy-preserving zk-SNARK-based framework to audit LLMs for post-deployment tampering using adversarial probes.
motivation: Post-deployment changes to LLMs can alter behavior while routine outputs appear unchanged, complicating AI governance when model weights are proprietary.
method: The authors propose using zk-SNARKs for verifiable audits without revealing model internals, and design three probe families (token-based, embedding-based, stress) to amplify logit drift.
result: Token-based probes show the strongest sensitivity; the zk-SNARK workflow scales practically, with proving time increasing modestly, verification time staying near constant, and proof size constant.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical approach for privacy-preserving auditing of LLMs, balancing sensitivity and deployment cost.

title: DisCTI: Who Needs To Know Timely? Automated Sector-Aware Cyber Threat Intelligence Dissemination
authors: Fajar Wijitrisnanto (national Cyber And Crypto Agency, Jakarta, Indonesia), Alsharif Abuadbba (CSIRO, Sydney, Australia), Yansong Gao (CSIRO, Sydney, Australia, The University Of Western Australia, Perth, Australia), Nan Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The timely dissemination of cyber threat intelligence (CTI) is critical for organizations to mount swift and effective incident response. When valid CTI is delivered to the right sector at the right time, identical attacks can often be contained or mitigated. However, today's rapidly expanding CTI landscape overwhelms analysts, who must sift through massive and heterogeneous feeds. Existing platforms such as the Malware Information Sharing Platform (MISP) provide sector tagging features (e.g., energy, finance, government), but in practice, these remain largely unmapped (98% of events are left uncategorized). This lack of automated and timely sector mapping severely limits the operational value of shared intelligence, leaving organizations that belong especially to the critical information infrastructure sector exposed. To address this gap, we formulate sector-targeted CTI dissemination as a multilabel classification problem. Leveraging deep field knowledge of CTI structures and sector-specific threat patterns, we construct a novel data set of 872 sector-labelled CTI events from a threat intelligence platform (TIP). We then apply BERT, a transformer-based model, to automate the mapping of CTI events to sectors. Using the structured threat information expression (STIX) format for cross-platform interoperability, our approach achieves a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.89 at a Hamming loss of 0.055 on the custom dataset, i.e. 94.5% of individual sector-label assignments are correct. These results not only demonstrate the feasibility of sector-aware, automated CTI dissemination but also highlight how embedding expert field knowledge into machine learning design fills a crucial gap in the threat intelligence pipeline, enabling faster and context-relevant defensive action.
tldr: This paper applies BERT-based multilabel classification to automate sector-tagged cyber threat intelligence dissemination, achieving high F1 scores on a custom dataset, but it is entirely unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The overwhelming volume of cyber threat intelligence and the lack of automated sector mapping hampers timely defensive actions, especially for critical infrastructure sectors.
method: The authors construct a dataset of 872 sector-labelled CTI events from a threat intelligence platform and train a BERT model to predict sector labels using the STIX format, framed as a multilabel classification problem.
result: The model achieves a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.89 and a Hamming loss of 0.055 on the custom dataset, with 94.5% of individual sector-label assignments correct.
conclusion: Automated sector-aware CTI dissemination is feasible and can significantly improve the operational value of shared threat intelligence, but this work has no connection to the user's research focus.

title: Moirae: A Multimodal Agent Collaborative Framework For Dynamic Android Malware Detection
authors: Xueying Zeng, Youquan Xian, Yanze Li, Bowen Hu, Ziqi Shan, Xu Luo, Danping Yang, Peng Liu, Lei Cui, Bo Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.27994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Android ecosystem faces persistent and rapidly evolving malware threats. Existing machine learning detectors are vulnerable to concept drift because they rely on implementation-specific features whose distributions change over time. Large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic understanding and zero-shot reasoning, but current LLM-based detectors typically depend on code-centric or single-dimensional evidence, making them susceptible to obfuscation and limiting comprehensive behavior analysis. We present {\sysname}, a multimodal agent collaborative framework for dynamic Android malware detection. {\sysname} dynamically collects multimodal runtime evidence and employs ReAct-based specialized agents to analyze complementary behavioral views. The detection process begins by identifying visual deception cues, modeling UI state transitions, and integrating runtime API behaviors to fuse multi-dimensional evidence across user-visible interfaces and hidden backend operations. Experiments on temporally and distributionally unseen datasets show that {\sysname} achieves an accuracy of 90.06\% without fine-tuning, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines and demonstrating strong zero-shot generalization against Android malware concept drift.
tldr: Proposes Moirae, a multimodal agent collaborative framework for dynamic Android malware detection that leverages LLM-based agents to analyze runtime evidence for robust zero-shot detection.
motivation: Existing ML-based Android malware detectors suffer from concept drift and are vulnerable to obfuscation, while LLM-based detectors often rely on single-dimensional evidence. A multimodal approach is needed to capture both visible and hidden behaviors.
method: Dynamically collects multimodal runtime evidence (visual deception cues, UI state transitions, runtime API behaviors) and uses ReAct-based specialized agents to fuse these complementary views for detection.
result: Achieves 90.06% accuracy on temporally and distributionally unseen malware datasets without fine-tuning, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
conclusion: Demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization against Android malware concept drift, suggesting that multimodal LLM-agent frameworks are promising for dynamic malware detection.

title: The Impact Of Magma: A Ground-Truth Fuzzing Benchmark
authors: Ahmad Hazimeh, Adrian Herrera, Srividya Subramanian, Thaqiya Aman, Sara Vaccino, Qiang Liu, Mathias Payer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magma is an open-source and ground-truth fuzzing benchmark that enables uniform fuzzer evaluation and comparison. Magma was originally released with a research paper published at ACM SIGMETRICS 2021. This short paper explains the motivation, the design, and the impact of Magma, with a description of extensions to the original benchmark.
tldr: This paper introduces Magma, an open-source ground-truth fuzzing benchmark for uniform evaluation of fuzzers.
motivation: To address the lack of a standardized and reproducible benchmark for comparing fuzzing tools.
method: The benchmark includes real-world vulnerabilities with ground truth, enabling consistent and fair fuzzer comparison.
result: Magma has achieved significant adoption as a standard benchmark in the fuzzing community.
conclusion: Magma provides a valuable resource for improving fuzzer evaluation and advancing software testing.

title: Compared To What? A Human-Anchored Security Benchmark For LLM-Generated Infrastructure-as-Code
authors: Animesh Shaw
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to author Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), where a single insecure default can be deployed directly into production. Prior evaluations report raw vulnerability counts for model-generated IaC, but without a human baseline they cannot determine whether models are actually worse than engineers. We introduce GenIaC-SecBench, a benchmark of 100 deployment scenarios stratified by architectural complexity, evaluated across 12 model configurations from four vendors, producing 1,196 IaC artifacts scanned by three independent policy engines (Checkov, Trivy, KICS). Critically, we also scan 634 human-authored IaC templates with the same toolchain, providing the first size-matched human security baseline. Vulnerability density is strongly inverse to artifact size (Spearman [MATH], [MATH]), meaning unmatched comparisons measure size rather than security. When matched on declared-resource count, all model configurations fall within 3.21x--3.87x the human vulnerability density, with the gap widening for simpler tasks (4.9x at one resource, 1.4x at twenty or more). We decompose reasoning into standard generation, prompt-engineered chain-of-thought, and vendor extended-thinking APIs. Vendor extended thinking significantly outperforms prompted chain-of-thought ([MATH], [MATH]), while prompted chain-of-thought is indistinguishable from standard generation ([MATH], n.s.). Token instrumentation shows extended thinking uses under 1\% of the output budget, explaining its bounded effect. Two negative results also emerge: deployability does not correlate with vulnerability ([MATH], [MATH]), and classical complete-case Friedman testing is infeasible for realistic benchmark designs, motivating the Skillings-Mack statistic. All code, data, and regeneration scripts are released.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark (GenIaC-SecBench) to compare security of LLM-generated Infrastructure-as-Code against a human baseline, finding models are about 3-5x worse in vulnerability density.
motivation: Prior evaluations of LLM-generated IaC lacked a human baseline, so it was unclear if models are actually worse than human engineers. This work aims to provide a size-matched human security baseline.
method: The authors created 100 deployment scenarios spanning architectural complexity, generated 1,196 IaC artifacts with 12 model configurations from 4 vendors, scanned them with Checkov, Trivy, and KICS, and compared against 634 human-authored templates using the same toolchain.
result: Vulnerability density inversely correlates with artifact size; after matching on resource count, all models fall within 3.21x-3.87x of human vulnerability density, with the gap widening for simpler tasks. Extended thinking APIs outperform prompted chain-of-thought, while prompted chain-of-thought is indistinguishable from standard generation.
conclusion: The paper provides a first human-anchored security benchmark for LLM-generated IaC, revealing that while models are not drastically worse, simpler tasks show larger gaps, and token instrumentation suggests extended thinking has limited impact. It also highlights statistical limitations of classical testing in such benchmarks.

title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark For Prompt Injection
authors: Yupei Liu, Yuqi Jia, Neil Zhenqiang Gong, Jinyuan Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection attacks pose a serious security risk to large language models in real-world applications. However, existing prompt injection benchmarks primarily focus on short-context inputs, leaving the attacks and defenses in long-context settings largely unexplored. This gap leads to a substantial overestimation of the effectiveness of current defenses. In this paper, we bridge the gap by introducing LongPIBench, a long-context benchmark for prompt injection covering 4 realistic application scenarios: paper peer review, resume screening, code review, and email summary. For each scenario, we construct a synthetic dataset and a real-world dataset, with context lengths ranging from thousands to tens of thousands of tokens. The evaluation results on LongPIBench reveal significant vulnerabilities of prompt injection defenses under long-context settings: even simple heuristic prompt injection attacks achieve high success rates and frequently bypass state-of-the-art defenses. We hope LongPIBench can serve as a practical benchmark for systematically evaluating prompt injection defenses in realistic long-context scenarios.
tldr: Introduces LongPIBench, a long-context benchmark for evaluating prompt injection attacks and defenses on large language models across realistic application scenarios.
motivation: Existing prompt injection benchmarks focus on short-context inputs, leading to overestimation of defense effectiveness; long-context settings remain unexplored.
method: Constructs a benchmark covering four realistic scenarios (paper review, resume screening, code review, email summary) with synthetic and real-world datasets, context lengths ranging from thousands to tens of thousands of tokens.
result: Evaluation reveals that even simple heuristic attacks achieve high success rates and frequently bypass state-of-the-art defenses in long-context settings.
conclusion: LongPIBench serves as a practical benchmark for systematically evaluating prompt injection defenses in realistic long-context scenarios.

title: Exploiting Per-Core Leakage: Electromagnetic Side-Channel Monitoring Of Multicore Architectures
authors: Daehyeon Bae, Sujin Park, Insup Lee, Younggiu Jung, Kyeongsik Lee, Heeseok Kim, Seokhie Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multicore processors are increasingly adopted in embedded systems to meet growing performance demands. However, physical side-channel analysis of multicore architectures remains underexplored, as obtaining usable leakage is inherently challenging. Consequently, side-channel security research on such systems has lagged far behind, leaving a critical security gap. To address this gap, we reveal the electromagnetic leakage mechanisms in multicore architectures and, for the first time, demonstrate per-core leakage exploitation, thereby enabling physical side-channel analysis for these systems. As a practical extension, we present a non-intrusive side-channel monitoring method that achieves per-core granularity. To validate its feasibility and practicality, we implement a prototype on a heterogeneous SoC platform with an RF front-end, and evaluate on a commercial off-the-shelf quad-core embedded system, the Raspberry Pi 4B with ARM Cortex-A72 cores.
tldr: This paper demonstrates per-core electromagnetic leakage exploitation in multicore processors, enabling physical side-channel analysis through a non-intrusive monitoring method.
motivation: Multicore processors are increasingly used but side-channel security research lags behind due to difficult leakage acquisition; the paper aims to fill this gap.
method: The authors reveal leakage mechanisms and propose a non-intrusive side-channel monitoring method achieving per-core granularity, implemented on a heterogeneous SoC with RF front-end.
result: Implementation on Raspberry Pi 4B (ARM Cortex-A72) validates feasibility and practicality.
conclusion: The work enables per-core physical side-channel analysis for multicore systems, addressing a critical security gap.

title: Distributed Cross-Layer Optimization For Covert Multi-Hop, Multi-Modal Networks: Exponentially Fast Convergence And Robust Tracking
authors: Sirin Chakraborty, Andrea Panebianco, Yuchen Tian, Kevin S Chan, Fikadu Dagefu, Yin Sun, Ness B. Shroff
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops the first distributed cross-layer algorithm for joint congestion control, routing, scheduling, and power control in covert multi-hop, multi-modal wireless networks, where adversarial wardens (Willies) monitor radio modalities via energy detection. The Detection Error Probability (DEP), the probability that a Willie fails to reliably detect ongoing transmissions, is generally non-concave in the transmit powers, making DEP-based covert network optimization challenging. We resolve this by constructing the tightest concave lower bound on the log-DEP, yielding a conservative convex problem that guarantees satisfaction of the original DEP constraints and unifies hard covertness constraints and covertness-utility maximization in a single problem. We develop a Parallel Proximal Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (PP-ADMM) algorithm for the resulting cross-layer problem and prove global Q-linear convergence, i.e., exponentially fast convergence, to the set of optimal solutions under standard regularity conditions. Numerical results confirm linear convergence and demonstrate robust tracking performance under channel fading and Willie mobility.
tldr: This paper presents a distributed cross-layer optimization algorithm for covert wireless networks, addressing covertness constraints via a convex approximation and proving exponential convergence.
motivation: Covert multi-hop wireless networks require joint optimization of congestion control, routing, scheduling, and power control to avoid detection by adversarial wardens, but the detection error probability is non-concave, making optimization challenging.
method: The authors construct the tightest concave lower bound on the log-DEP to form a conservative convex problem, then develop a Parallel Proximal Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (PP-ADMM) algorithm to solve it.
result: They prove global Q-linear convergence to the optimal solution set under standard regularity conditions and demonstrate robust tracking under channel fading and Willie mobility with numerical results.
conclusion: The work provides the first distributed cross-layer algorithm for covert multi-modal networks with guaranteed exponential convergence, enabling efficient and secure communication in adversarial environments.
